title: Davis scores the go-ahead goal in Boston's 2-1 victory over Racing Louisville
summary: Deja Davis scored on a header early in the second half and the Boston Legacy downed Racing Louisville 2-1 in the National Women’s Soccer League on Friday night
story: Deja Davis scored on a header early in the second half and the Boston Legacy downed Racing Louisville 2-1 in the National Women’s Soccer League on Friday night
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- Deja Davis scored on a header early in the second half and the Boston Legacy downed Racing Louisville 2-1 in the National Women's Soccer League on Friday night.
Boston (9-14-5) has four wins in the last six games but has already been eliminated from the playoffs.
Racing Louisville (7-18-3) is winless in its last eight games and has also been eliminated from the postseason.
After a rain delay of more than an hour at Gillette Stadium, the Legacy went ahead in the ninth minute on Amanda Gutierres' goal off a well-placed cross from Bianca St-Georges.
Kayla Fischer scored the equalizer for Louisville in the 22nd, capitalizing on a mistake by Boston goalkeeper Laurel Ivory. Fisher leads Racing with eight goals this season.
Davis scored Boston's go-ahead goal in the 51st minute. It was her first career NWSL goal.
Emma Sears' header for Racing in stoppage time flew over goal in a final bid to salvage a point.
The Legacy acquired forward Gift Monday last week from the Washington Spirit, but she was not available because of international duty.
Boston was without starting goalkeeper Casey Murphy, who was placed on the season-ending injury list this week with torn posterior cruciate ligament in her left knee.

title: TJ Smith has pick-6 as Tulane forces 6 turnovers in 31-17 victory over Memphis
summary: TJ Smith returned an interception 76 yards for a touchdown on the final play of the first half, and Johnnie Daniels raced 48 yards for a score on a fourth-and-1 run with 1:34 remaining as Tulane forced six turnovers in a 31-17 victory over Memphis
story: TJ Smith returned an interception 76 yards for a touchdown on the final play of the first half, and Johnnie Daniels raced 48 yards for a score on a fourth-and-1 run with 1:34 remaining as Tulane forced six turnovers in a 31-17 victory over Memphis

NEW ORLEANS -- TJ Smith returned an interception 76 yards for a touchdown on the final play of the first half, and Johnnie Daniels raced 48 yards for a score on a fourth-and-1 run with 1:34 remaining as Tulane forced six turnovers in a 31-17 victory over Memphis on Friday night.
Freshman Trace Johnson completed 11 for 21 passes for 165 yards for Tulane (3-3, 1-1 American Conference) in his first collegiate start — with a touchdown pass and an interception.
Philippe Laforge kicked a 44-yard field goal to give Memphis (5-2, 2-1) the lead on its first possession.

Johnson and Tulane picked up two first downs after going three-and-out on its first three drives, leading to a 56-yard field goal by redshirt freshman Cooper Helmke to tie it 12 seconds into the second quarter.
Marcus Stokes completed a short pass two plays later to Stonka Burnside, who turned it into a 76-yard touchdown and Memphis led 10-3.
Helmke made a 40-yarder to cut it to 10-6 with 6:47 left before halftime.

The Green Wave, who forced one turnover in their first five games, recovered their third fumble of the game to begin a drive at the 50-yard line. Johnson had his first touchdown pass three plays later — a 38-yarder to Destyn Hill — for a 13-10 lead.
Helmke added a 29-yard field goal before Smith's pick-6 for a 23-10 lead at halftime.

After a scoreless third quarter, Stokes connected with Jemyri Davis for a 6-yard touchdown with 3:34 remaining to cut it to 23-17. The Tigers got the ball back, but Kevin Adams III picked off his second pass to seal the victory.

Stokes finished with 306 yards on 20-for-37 passing with two scores and four interceptions. He also lost two of his three fumbles. Jaylin Carter had 135 yards on 23 rushes and Burnside totaled 151 yards on seven receptions.
Tulane last forced six turnovers in a 34-7 victory over FCS member Jackson State in the 2013 season opener.
Memphis: Hosts East Carolina on Thursday.
Tulane: Hosts UTSA on Oct. 24.

title: It's over: Canada ends England's unbeaten streak in women's rugby with a 24-21 win
summary: A month after Canada halted England’s 39-match winning streak in women’s rugby, it has also ended its 40-match unbeaten streak
story: A month after Canada halted England’s 39-match winning streak in women’s rugby, it has also ended its 40-match unbeaten streak
TORONTO -- A month after Canada halted England's 39-match winning streak in women's rugby, it also ended its 40-match unbeaten streak Friday.
The Canadians came back from a 14-5 halftime deficit and took the lead when center Shoshanah Seumanutafa scored a try with three minutes remaining to give the home side a 24-21 win.
The match was played before 18,621 spectators at BMO Field in Toronto, which organizers said was a North American record for a stand-alone women’s match.

At Exeter, England on Sept. 19, Canada ended England’s record 39-match winning streak with a 26-26 draw, part of the WXV Global Series. It was their first match against each other since England won the final of the 2025 Women’s Rugby World Cup a year ago.
England hadn’t lost since dropping a 34-31 decision to New Zealand in the 2022 World Cup final nearly four years ago. After its draw with Canada, England beat New Zealand in another WXV match.

Fullback Savannah Bauder scored an opening try for Canada in the 17th minute Friday after a series of passes. But captain Sophie de Goede missed the conversion attempt, and until Canada's late try, that proved to be the difference in the match.
England took the lead in the 32nd minute with a converted try by Maddie Feaunati, and flyhalf Zoe Harrison scored a second try five minutes later to leave England with its 14-5 lead at halftime.
Canada and England will play again next Friday in Ottawa.

title: ALCS Game 4 postponed by rain; Rays and Guardians to resume series Saturday
summary: Game 4 of the American League Championship Series has been postponed because of rain
story: Game 4 of the American League Championship Series has been postponed because of rain
CLEVELAND -- Game 4 of the American League Championship Series between the Tampa Bay Rays and Cleveland Guardians was postponed because of rain Friday night.
Major League Baseball was hoping there would be a three-hour window of dry weather to get the game in, but the showers never let up.

“It never cleared out the way they were hoping. It started to get later in the hour, and MLB and I think both clubs did everything they could to try to get it in,” Rays manager Kevin Cash said. “Made the most sense, like, at this point and this hour, with no guarantee that there wasn’t another band coming.”
The teams will resume their playoff series Saturday at 8 p.m. ET, with Game 5 also at Progressive Field on Sunday at 5 p.m., and Game 6, if necessary, on Monday at 8 p.m. in St. Petersburg, Florida.

“We knew how many days ago that today was going to be a challenge. Numerous weather calls, numerous back and forths, and ultimately MLB decided we needed to wait it out,” Guardians manager Stephen Vogt said. “Obviously it’s an important game, and we need to make sure we’re doing everything we can to play the games when they’re scheduled. But MLB ultimately decided to wait this one out.”
It is the first time an ALCS game has been postponed since 2019, when the New York Yankees were hosting the Houston Astros.
The Guardians have a 2-1 lead in the best-of-seven series after Petey Halpin’s two-run homer propelled them to a 3-2 victory in Game 3 on Thursday afternoon.
Both teams will stick with their scheduled Game 4 starters from Friday. Cleveland will go with a bullpen game, with Shawn Armstrong being the opener. Nick Martinez will pitch for Tampa Bay.
It will be Armstrong’s fifth appearance this postseason. The right-hander has allowed only one hit in 5 1/3 innings with five strikeouts.
Armstrong thought his season was done in late July when he strained a calf muscle, but he returned during the final week of the regular season.

Armstrong was drafted by Cleveland in the 18th round in 2011 and made his big league debut four years later. He was traded to Seattle in 2017 and spent time with four other organizations, including Tampa Bay, before signing with the Guardians this season.

“I think I said it to (Erik) Sabrowski, whenever we were standing in the outfield in Game 2 in Tampa — obviously I played here, I got drafted here, coming back here and being able to be in this situation is — words can’t describe it,” Armstrong said before Game 3 on Thursday.

Martinez started Game 3 of the Division Series against the New York Yankees. He went 3 2/3 innings, allowing two runs on five hits with a walk and three strikeouts. The right-hander was 15-6 during the regular season and ranked sixth in the AL with a 3.10 ERA. He was third in the AL with 26 starts in which he allowed three runs or fewer.
“It’s just like my starts throughout the year; it’s going to be a dogfight going in, just to see how many outs I can get for this team. It’s important,” he said Thursday.

The teams might have to play the final four games of the series without a day off, culminating in a potential Game 7 on Tuesday. That could be welcome news for the Milwaukee Brewers, who have a week off before they open the World Series at home on Oct. 23 against the Cleveland-Tampa Bay winner.

Milwaukee is in the Fall Classic for the first time since 1982 after completing a four-game sweep of the two-time defending World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers in the NL Championship Series on Thursday night.
“We’ve got four games in a row. We have an opportunity to win some games and move on. And that’s all we’re focused on,” Vogt said.

title: Ansel Haugsjaa, Chevonne Forgan win 2 titles at USA Luge's national start championships
summary: Ansel Haugsjaa and Chevonne Forgan went to the Olympics last winter as doubles sliders
story: Ansel Haugsjaa and Chevonne Forgan went to the Olympics last winter as doubles sliders
LAKE PLACID, N.Y. -- Ansel Haugsjaa and Chevonne Forgan went to the Olympics last winter as doubles sliders. They did just fine on their own in the season's opening race.

Haugsjaa and Forgan pulled off rare feats by claiming titles in both singles and doubles races at USA Luge's national start championships, which are considered the unofficial start of the team's competitive season.

It was a night for doubles sliders to shine. Haugsjaa took the men's singles crown, then paired with Olympic teammate Marcus Mueller — who was second in the singles race, tied with fellow doubles specialist Zack DiGregorio — for their second national men's doubles start title in the last three years. Forgan claimed the women's singles title, before joining her Olympic teammate Sophia Kirkby to successfully defend their doubles start title.

“Showing up first and second in the singles race, we were feeling good going into doubles,” Haugsjaa said. “I was shocked by how comfortable and easy it felt going back on the doubles sled after doing singles. Felt like I was right back at home, so it was really nice.”

Mueller and Haugsjaa, who were world champions at the junior level, led the Olympic doubles race at Cortina d'Ampezzo, Italy in February, before a mistake in the second run sent them to a sixth-place finish.
Their success in singles on Friday doesn't have them thinking about trying those races more often.

“I think we're going to stick with doubles,” Mueller said. “We made that decision a few years ago, to stick with doubles because we thought we can do a lot better. And with how close it was in these recent Olympics, I think we're really going to go for gold.”
Same goes for Forgan, whose singles win seemed to catch her by surprise.
“Singles is scary,” Forgan said. “Singles definitely poses interesting challenges.”

A slew of past champions and Olympic veterans were not in Friday's race. Tucker West, a 13-time national start champion, retired after last season. Olympic women's singles racer Summer Britcher did not slide while recovering from injury, and longtime U.S. team member and Olympic veteran Emily Fischnaller has not revealed her future plans.
The World Cup season starts Nov. 28-29 in Winterberg, Germany.

title: LeBron James tosses chalk, gets 76ers intro for 1st time in Philadelphia in front of roaring fans
summary: LeBron James performed his famed chalk toss and was introduced to a roaring ovation on Friday night in his first preseason game for the 76ers in Philadelphia
story: LeBron James performed his famed chalk toss and was introduced to a roaring ovation on Friday night in his first preseason game for the 76ers in Philadelphia
PHILADELPHIA -- LeBron James performed his famed chalk toss and was introduced to a roaring ovation on Friday night in his first preseason game for the 76ers in Philadelphia.

The 41-year-old James, who joined the 76ers this summer for his NBA-record 24th season, brought the crowd to its feet early when he finished a dunk against the Boston Celtics off a half-court lob pass from All-Star Tyrese Maxey.
Just wait until it counts.
Public address announcer Matt Cord offered a full-throated “At 6-9, from St. Vincent-St. Mary’s, No. 23, LeBron James! James!” for the intros. Joel Embiid still got the final introduction.

While nothing from this game will go down on James' stat sheet, Sixers fans had been waiting to catch a glimpse of him in his No. 23 jersey since he signed with the team in July. Scores of kids in Sixers jerseys crowded over the home team entrance canopy and screamed for James to stop for a picture or an autograph.

The arena ushers behind the Sixers' bench kept saying “Keep walking!” to the gaggle of fans and slow walkers who stopped to watch James in warmups. One constantly barked, “You can't stand here unless you've got a ticket!”
None of the stragglers had one.
James did welcome one boy and one girl to the bench with him after he finished shooting and posed for a quick photo.
The Sixers played all of their starters except for VJ Edgecombe. Jaylen Brown played against the Celtics for the first time since the 2024 NBA Finals MVP was traded to the Sixers in the offseason.
James sat out the Sixers' home preseason opener but played in a scrimmage that was open to the public and drew 10,000 fans.
He then made his preseason debut last week at Brooklyn. He had 10 points, five assists and four rebounds in the first half.

The Sixers play their season opener on Tuesday against New York at Madison Square Garden, where the Knicks will raise the banner to celebrate their NBA championship. Philadelphia's home opener is Thursday against Cleveland, followed by back-to-back games over the weekend.
James spent the last eight seasons with the Los Angeles Lakers before signing a two-year deal with the Sixers for the league minimum.

title: Shohei Ohtani's health and a possible lockout loom over an uncertain offseason for the Dodgers
summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers face uncertainty after their earliest postseason exit in three years
story: The Los Angeles Dodgers face uncertainty after their earliest postseason exit in three years
LOS ANGELES -- After their earliest postseason exit in three years, the Los Angeles Dodgers head into the offseason facing uncertainty over next year.

Shohei Ohtani was dogged by injuries to his left knee and right biceps over the second half and into the playoffs that rendered him ineffective at the plate. The two-way superstar also didn't pitch after the All-Star break.

Whether Ohtani needs offseason surgery remains to be seen, although he acknowledged it's possible after Thursday's loss to the Brewers that completed Milwaukee's sweep of the NL Championship Series. If he does, would the recovery bleed into the start of next season?

A potential MLB lockout is looming with the current collective bargaining agreement set to expire on Dec. 1. Team owners have proposed a salary cap — something the sport has never had — and the players' union has adamantly rejected the idea.

A work stoppage would give Ohtani extra time to heal, although during such time the Dodgers would be cut off from communicating with any player, leaving Ohtani to rehab either from possible surgery or from his injuries on his own.

Communication between Ohtani and the team on his health during the season was “awesome,” Andrew Friedman, president of baseball operations, said last month, but he added: “The fully sharing exactly how he's feeling, maybe not so awesome.”
Ohtani said he plans to resume pitching next year, when he'll turn 33 in July. He's already had two Tommy John surgeries.
“What he’s doing is unprecedented, and it takes a real toll,” Friedman said. “And as you get older, I think us just being very dialed is going to be really important.”

The Dodgers had baseball's second-highest opening day payroll this year at $323.3 million, behind the New York Mets at $358.4 million. If a salary cap were to be imposed, the Dodgers' spending would be constrained when play resumes.

Some of the roster could look different next year, too, with nine players set to become free agents after the World Series, led by two-time Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal, who is expected to command a huge deal.

The Dodgers acquired Skubal from Detroit just before the trade deadline in August. The left-hander was 5-2 with a 2.61 ERA and 70 strikeouts in 10 regular-season games for his new team. In the postseason, he was 1-1 with a 2.45 ERA and 14 Ks. Skubal didn't want to discuss his future Thursday, although he expressed enthusiasm for the organization, his teammates and the fans.
Other impending free agents are infielder Miguel Rojas, utility player Kiké Hernández, and relievers Kris Bubic, Brusdar Graterol, Eric Lauer, Evan Phillips, Blake Treinen and Alex Vesia.
As expected, Rojas announced his retirement Thursday, saying, “This is it, guys. That was my last game played.” He'll still be around, though, to work in a player development role.

The Dodgers got a glimpse of the future when they promoted Josue De Paula directly from Double-A to the majors in September. His energy and at-bats at designated hitter during Ohtani's stint on the injured list made an impression, and the 21-year-old was added to the postseason roster as a pinch-hitter.

The team will look to De Paula to further improve as an outfielder in 2027, although finding playing time for him will be challenging given the trio of veteran starters: Teoscar Hernández, Andy Pages and Kyle Tucker. De Paula is also blocked at DH by Ohtani.

“I think the experience he got being up here and watching what our guys do on a daily basis just helped connect some dots for him,” Friedman said. “And so, physically, he is capable of being a good corner outfielder, and we’re going to continue to tap into that.”

Mookie Betts, Freddie Freeman, Ohtani, Tucker, Max Muncy and Will Smith will remain the Dodgers' veteran core. But some supporting players could be offloaded, like Kiké Hernández. Playing on a one-year deal, the 35-year-old was limited to 41 games while recovering from injuries and he didn't provide his usual postseason pop.
Manager Dave Roberts refused to blame an aging lineup for getting swept by the Brewers, whose 103 regular-season wins were three more than the Dodgers.
“We got beat,” he said. “There’s no because we’re too old or whatever. Every facet of the game, if you kind of unpack it, we were bested.”
There's drama off the field, too.

Owner Mark Walter was noticeably absent from the team's playoff games. He is facing multiple federal investigations into his business empire for possible financial improprieties involving insurance companies he controls. Walter has denied any wrongdoing. Since August, he sold his controlling interest in the Los Angeles Lakers and last month he unloaded his share in Chelsea of the Premier League.

title: Raimondo scores hat trick for Frosinone in Italy. Frankfurt ends winless drought at home
summary: Eintracht Frankfurt has ended its six-game winless streak at home thanks a slender and hard-fought win over Cologne
story: Eintracht Frankfurt has ended its six-game winless streak at home thanks a slender and hard-fought win over Cologne

Antonio Raimondo scored a hat trick for Frosinone in a 4-2 win over Sassuolo in Serie A on Friday, and Toulouse netted three times in the second half to overcome a plucky Le Mans 3-0 in the French league.
Younes Ebnoutalib’s late goal gave Eintracht Frankfurt a 1-0 win over Cologne and ended its six-game winless run at home in the Bundesliga.
In Spain, lowly Levante picked up points for the second game in a row when it came from behind to draw 1-1 at Deportivo La Coruna.
In Germany, neither side created many chances but Ebnoutalib finished neatly in the 77th minute after being set up by Noëll Aséko Nkili, who had replaced Mario Götze moments earlier.
The result was a welcome win for a side that lost 6-0 at Leipzig in its last game and which lifts it into eighth place.
Cologne fell to 11th after a 16th straight away game without a win, the longest current streak in the Bundesliga.

Giacomo Calo opened the scoring for Frosinone with the aid of a goalkeeping error and although Domenico Berardi equalized for the visitors after a quarter of an hour, Raimundo took charge soon after with a series of classic poacher goals.
The striker on loan from Bologna scored in the 26th and 30th minutes and added a fourth in the second half after Kristian Thorstvedt had cut the deficit.
It marked seven goals in seven games for the 22-year-old Raimondo, coming after doubles against Fiorentina and Venezia before the international break.
The win got Frosinone back on track after a 3-0 loss to Napoli last weekend and lifts it into fifth place in the Serie A table.
Sassuolo is 11th and has now failed to keep a clean sheet in all seven of its Serie A games this season.
Toulouse used a dominant second half to end Le Mans unbeaten home run in Ligue 1.
Back in the top tier after 16 years, Le Mans had not lost in its first three home matches this season.

But a 46th-minute goal from Canadian striker Jacen Russell-Rowe put Toulouse in front and Norwegian midfielder Aron Donnum added a second on the hour mark. Dane Casper Tengstedt netted the third in the 87th.
Le Mans has now conceded goals in all seven of its league games this season.
The newly promoted side sits in 15th place, while Toulouse moved into seventh.
Daniel Requena’s first goal of the season earned Levante a draw at Deportivo La Coruna and extended the home side’s winless run to five matches.
Coruna started the season with an unbeaten run of five games but it hasn’t won since.
It took the lead through Cameroon forward Bil Nsongo after 63 minutes but Requena’s equalized eight minutes from the end.
Levante has now taken four points from its last six and moved one point further from the bottom three.
Coruna remained in eighth with 11 points.

title: Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries are top defensive teams in WNBA, now facing off in finals
summary: The two best defensive teams in the WNBA are about the meet for the title
story: The two best defensive teams in the WNBA are about the meet for the title
SAN FRANCISCO -- Golden State forward Kayla Thornton knows every basket in the WNBA Finals will be tough to come by, given how much the Valkyries and the Atlanta Dream take pride in making stops.

The league's two best defensive teams are about to square off for a championship in a best-of-seven series that could be low-scoring. The Valkyries host Game 1 on Saturday with their raucous “Ballhalla” home crowd to back them on the biggest stage this second-year franchise has reached.
“We’re the top two in the league,” Thornton said, “so I think it comes down to just the details and who wants it more.”

Dream star Angel Reese loves to get involved in every play and wreak havoc, whether by forcing jump balls or making steals. The Dream have four of the top seven players in steals this postseason, led by Jordan Canada and Rhyne Howard at 2.2 per game. Golden State's Gabby Williams is averaging 1.7 steals in the playoffs, while Reese has a 1.6 steals average.
“They like to get in the passing lanes,” Williams said. “It’s maybe going to be a game where good offense leads to good defense.”

Atlanta is chasing the first championship in franchise history after losing in the Finals three times in four years from 2010-13. Atlanta lost in the first round the past three seasons but enters this series on a 10-game winning streak dating to the final game before the break for the women's FIBA World Cup.
The Dream swept Washington and New York in the playoffs.
“Nobody thought that we would make it to the Finals and we’re doing that, we’re achieving that,” Howard said. “We set out goals long before this year and it’s finally coming into fruition.”

Dream forward Allisha Gray took part in a light practice on Friday and will be a game-time decision for Game 1 after missing the last two games of the semifinal series with an injured left ring finger.
“We’re just waiting to see how my finger reacts to just the pace and intensity of the practice, and then we’ll know,” Gray said.
Coach Karl Smesko said he's hopeful Gray will be able to play at some point in the series.
Gray led the team in scoring in the regular season at 19 points per game and is the best outside shooter for Atlanta with 3.1 3-pointers per game.
“It’s definitely hard because you want to be out there and compete with your teammates,” she said. “But I’ll say it just gave me time to rest my body and get healthy.”

The Valkyries are the fastest expansion team to reach the WNBA Finals by getting there in year two — one year faster than Atlanta did in 2010. They did it by eliminating the defending champion Las Vegas Aces in the semifinals.

Other expansion teams have had quick success like Golden State. The NHL's Vegas Golden Knights reached the Stanley Cup Final in their inaugural season in 2017-18 and the Chicago Fire won the Major League Soccer title in their first season in 1998.

But the Valkyries have a chance to set a record. The fastest expansion champion in the modern era for the WNBA, NFL, NHL, NBA and MLB was the Milwaukee Bucks, who won the NBA Finals in their third season in 1970-71.

The magnitude of the moment doesn't seem to faze Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase, who was on Becky Hammon's Las Vegas staff when the Aces won back-to-back titles in 2022 and ‘23. Nakase served as an assistant for the champion U.S. team in last month’s FIBA World Cup in Berlin.
“It’s not just me, I don’t feel alone in this at all,” she said. “I feel like this is going to be a collective effort about us putting all of our high IQs together.”

The Valkyries have plenty of championship-tested players who can offer some insight. Thornton won it all with the Liberty in 2024. Kiah Stokes earned rings with the Aces under Nakase in 2022 and '23 then another last year. Cecilia Zandalasini won a title with Minnesota in 2017.
Stokes is averaging 9.5 rebounds this postseason, ranking her third and top among players in the finals. Reese is next among players from these teams at 8.4 rebounds.

The Dream have three players who have won WNBA titles with DeWanna Bonner doing it in 2009 and ‘14 with Phoenix, Jordin Canada in 2018 and ’20 with Seattle, and Shatori Walker-Kimbrough in 2019 with Washington.
Many of Golden State's stars — including Williams — have been cast off by other teams, giving them more reason to want to show what they can do.

“A lot of people on our team have just felt undervalued or unappreciated or if you're not the main star on your team you kind of get overlooked,” Stokes said. “A lot of players have that mindset so coming to a team where it's kind of like a clean slate, Natalie, she's not going to BS you, if you don't do your job you're not going to play.”
AP Sports Writer Josh Dubow contributed to this report.

title: Jonathon Cooper is back for the Broncos, but the NFL’s personal conduct review isn’t over
summary: NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell has removed Denver Broncos pass rusher Jonathon Cooper from the league's exempt list
story: NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell has removed Denver Broncos pass rusher Jonathon Cooper from the league's exempt list

ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- ENGLEWOOD, Colo. (AP) — Denver Broncos pass rusher Jonathon Cooper was removed Friday from the commissioner's exempt list, which had kept him out of the team's first six games. He'll be eligible to play in the Broncos' next game at Arizona on Oct. 25.

The league said its review of Cooper’s conduct for potential violation of its personal conduct policy after a pair of domestic violence arrests in June remains ongoing and is unaffected by Cooper’s status change.
Cooper faces numerous charges, including one of felony strangulation of his then-girlfriend. His trial has been scheduled for March 2-4.

“Playing in the NFL and representing the Denver Broncos is a privilege I do not take for granted,” Cooper posted on Instagram shortly after his reinstatement. "I'm grateful to ownership, my teammates, coaches and everyone in the organization for their support as well as Commissioner (Roger) Goodell and the league for the opportunity to return.

“Over the last several months, I've spent a lot of time working to better myself. That work will continue,” Cooper added. “My focus is on being the best person, father, teammate and member of this community I can be. I will show that commitment through my actions every day.”

Cooper was placed on the exempt list on Aug. 30 and missed Denver's first six games. The Broncos are coming off a 17-14 win over the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday night that improved their record to 4-2.

Cooper, 28, was arrested on June 4 following an argument and physical confrontation with his then-girlfriend that eventually resulted in a felony charge of strangulation. He was arrested again a week later after violating a protection order by trying to contact the woman, according to the arrest affidavit.

If Cooper is ultimately suspended by the league, his six-week absence would essentially be time already served up to six games. But he would have to repay any game checks he received while on the exempt list because suspended players can't be paid. If any suspension exceeds six games, he'd have to miss more games.

Cooper, who's making $12 million this season, had been allowed to attend meetings and work out at team headquarters but was ineligible to practice during his time on the exempt list. He can resume practicing under a one-week roster exemption when the team returns from a long weekend next week.

Cooper's replacement in the starting lineup, Jonah Ellis, appeared to suffer a potentially serious injury in the final minute of regulation Thursday night when he was rushing Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold. Ellis' right leg bent back awkwardly on the play and he hopped to the sideline, never putting any weight on his right leg.
The Broncos have provided no updates on the status of Ellis, who had one of five sacks of Darnold on Thursday night.

title: Two of MLB's smallest spenders will meet in the World Series for first time since 1991
summary: For the first time since 1991, two teams with bottom-half payrolls will meet in the World Series
story: For the first time since 1991, two teams with bottom-half payrolls will meet in the World Series

NEW YORK -- When the Milwaukee Brewers defeated the mighty, monied Los Angeles Dodgers on Thursday night, it set up the first World Series between two of baseball’s smallest spenders in 35 years — just as team owners are arguing that such clubs need a salary cap to compete consistently.

Milwaukee will face Cleveland or Tampa Bay in a best-of-seven series for the title beginning Oct. 23, ensuring two clubs in the bottom half of big league payrolls will play in the World Series for the first time since 1991. The Dodgers, New York Mets and New York Yankees will watch from home with payrolls this season that each cost more than the Brewers', Guardians' and Rays' rosters combined.

The low-budget World Series showdown will start six weeks before a likely management lockout, a work stoppage that threatens the 2027 season as owners and players battle over the sport's lack of a salary cap.
Speaking at the All-Star Game in July, Major League Baseball Commissioner Rob Manfred made his case for a cap while saying exceptions did not reflect parity.

“Our view of the world is that over a very long period of time there’s a very strong relationship between who gets into the playoffs and who proceeds, notwithstanding the exceptions we’ve got," he said.

Milwaukee, which won the National League pennant with a four-game sweep of the Dodgers, had MLB’s 19th-highest payroll as of Aug. 31, while Tampa Bay was 25th and Cleveland 30th. The last time both pennant winners were among the bottom 50% in player spending was when Minnesota (15th among 26 teams) beat Atlanta (19th) for the 1991 championship.

In terms of market size, Milwaukee ranks as MLB’s 30th and smallest Designated Market Area, defined by Nielsen as non-overlapping geographic regions that group counties based on television viewing areas. Cleveland is 22nd and Tampa Bay 15th.

If the Guardians win the AL pennant, it would mark the first World Series involving two teams in the bottom half of MLB cities by DMA since St. Louis (24th) beat Detroit (18th) in 2006. No small-market team has won the World Series since Kansas City in 2015.

Three years after the Twins won that 1991 title, players went on strike as owners pushed for a salary cap, leading to the cancellation of the World Series. No such cap was added, and owners hadn't proposed one again until this summer.
Since the 1991 Twins, the only World Series winners with bottom-half payrolls have been the 2002 Anaheim Angels, 2003 Florida Marlins and 2017 Houston Astros.

“It's how the game is played in the moment dictates winning outcomes,” agent Scott Boras said Friday. “There’s no question that the probabilities of winning, success, are increased with greater talent, but we all know that talent has many variables as to how it performs at times.”
MLB owners have proposed a salary cap with a floor, a system players say they will never accept. A lockout is likely to start Dec. 2.

Opening-day payrolls were topped by the Mets ($358.4 million), Dodgers ($323.3 million) and Yankees ($302.8 million). The Brewers were at $125.9 million, the Rays $90.5 million and the Guardians $75.5 million.

“Don't believe what you hear from the owner who’s complaining, 'I don’t have the resources to compete,'" players' association head Bruce Meyer said at the All-Star Game. “They all have the resources to compete. Our proposals include provisions that would give them more resources and reward the teams that actually do compete.”
Manfred maintains spending big increases the odds of success.

“It defies human experience to ask a fan to think that the bottom end of that gap has the same opportunity to win as the top,” he said. “There is no question that everybody in any sport is not going to win once every 30 or 32 years depending on how many teams you have, but the data in our sport is stark: Your opportunity to make the playoffs if you are a larger-market team is dramatically higher and your opportunity to proceed to the subsequent rounds, that advantage grows with each round.”

title: Wall-to-wall Top 25 showdowns, with 6 ranked matchups on tap starting with Ohio State at Indiana
summary: Week 7 of college football is packed with excitement as six games feature teams ranked in the AP Top 25
story: Week 7 of college football is packed with excitement as six games feature teams ranked in the AP Top 25
Week 7 of the college football season is teed up to be one of the best so far, with six games pitting teams ranked in The Associated Press Top 25.

The showdowns are also scheduled just the way a fan at home with the remote might ask for: Two noon Eastern games, two more at 3:30 p.m. and the final pairing kicking off at 7:30 p.m. A look at the wall-to-wall coverage:

— No. 4 Ohio State (5-1) visits No. 5 Indiana (6-0) in a meeting of the last two national champions. The winner gains the inside track for a spot in the Big Ten championship game and also will get a bump in College Football Playoff seeding consideration.

Lots of eyeballs will be on three of the best receivers in the country: Ohio State’s Jeremiah Smith has put up prodigious numbers and is the Heisman Trophy frontrunner while Indiana has the nation’s top tandem in Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh.

Indiana enters the game with the Bowl Subdivision’s longest active winning streak (22 games) and the nation’s longest active home winning streak (19). But the Hoosiers haven't beaten Ohio State in Bloomington since 1987 and are 3 1/2-point underdogs at home.
— No. 16 Mississippi State (4-1) goes to No. 22 LSU (4-2), and a Bulldogs win would all but end LSU’s hopes of making the playoff in Lane Kiffin’s first season. The Tigers are favored by 15 1/2.
— No. 6 Alabama (5-1) and No. 14 Tennessee (5-1) resume their "Third Saturday in October" rivalry in Knoxville.

Tennessee gave up 10 sacks in a three-point loss to Texas and freshman quarterback Faizon Brandon has been restricted by a shoulder injury, which means sophomore George MacIntyre was prepping for the ferocious Alabama defense, which has nine interceptions already this season. The Crimson Tide will be missing star receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams but are favored by 7 1/2.

— No. 9 Mississippi (4-1) hosts No. 13 Missouri (5-1) in a homecoming of sorts for Tigers quarterback Austin Simmons. He began last season as Mississippi’s starter and gave way to Trinidad Chambliss, who still holds the job in Oxford. Ole Miss is a 5 1/2-point favorite.

— No. 2 Notre Dame (6-0) plays at No. 8 BYU (5-0) in the first top-10 game in LaVell Edwards Stadium history. It's something of a “prove it” game for two teams with underwhelming schedules and a win here helps burnish CFP seeding credentials.

Preseason Heisman favorite CJ Carr has 16 touchdown passes for the Fighting Irish against one interception and is averaging 229 yards passing per game on 70% accuracy. BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier has carried a heavier load since star RB LJ Martin got hurt but he passed for 329 yards and ran for 109 yards last week against Iowa State going into this one against a stout defense. Notre Dame is favored by 10 1/2.
— No. 18 Oklahoma St. (4-1) visits No. 20 Houston (5-1) in a game between two teams eager to crash the Big 12 party.

The Cowboys were awful the last two years and now, with 91 newcomers and first-year coach Eric Morris, have become one of the feel-good stories of the season after losing to Tulsa and starting their current four-game win streak with an upset of Oregon. Led by Drew Mestemaker, the Cowboys top the Big 12 and rank sixth in the nation by averaging 521.4 yards a game.

The Cougars’ only loss was a nailbiter to Texas Tech. Houston ranks third in the conference and 12th in the nation with 481.8 yards a game, with Conner Weigman's 15 touchdown passes second-most in the league. Houston is favored by 4 1/2.
Rutgers (1-4) visits Maryland (2-4) and may the best coach win.

The Scarlet Knights’ only win so far was against Howard while the Terrapins have beaten Hampton and UConn. This has left the job security for both Rutgers' Greg Schiano and Maryland's Mike Locksley as tenuous at best.

Locksley is the only coach on a hotter seat than Schiano, according to rankings by CoachesHotSeat.com. No athletic department wants to pay a buyout and do a coaching search in the middle of the season, but anything is possible. Locksley would be owed $9.7 million and Schiano about $18 million, according to media reports.
Maryland is favored by 5 1/2.

title: NFL will remove Packers' Josh Jacobs from commissioner's exempt list. He can play again on Oct. 25
summary: Green Bay running back Josh Jacobs is getting removed from the commissioner's exempt list and will be eligible to play again Oct. 25 when the Packers visit the Detroit Lions
story: Green Bay running back Josh Jacobs is getting removed from the commissioner's exempt list and will be eligible to play again Oct. 25 when the Packers visit the Detroit Lions
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs is getting removed from the commissioner's exempt list and will be eligible to play again Oct. 25 at Detroit.

The NFL announced Friday that Jacobs would be removed from the list on Monday, although the league's investigation of him under its personal conduct policy continues unaffected by the change to his roster status.

Jacobs has missed the Packers' first five games and also won't be available for their Sunday night matchup with the Dallas Cowboys at Lambeau Field. The NFL started investigating Jacobs after his arrest in May, which followed an altercation with Jacobs’ then-girlfriend.
Jacobs’ lawyers — Clarence F. Duchac III, David Z. Chesnoff and Richard A. Schonfeld — issued a statement on his behalf following the NFL’s announcement.

“Josh has dedicated the last several months to bettering himself, and he accepts responsibility for his actions,” they said. “He is excited to get back to work and on the field with his teammates. Josh is grateful for the support he is receiving from his teammates, coaches, the Packers organization, and the greatest fans in the world. Since there are ongoing legal matters, he will not have any further comment.”

Jacobs pleaded no contest last month to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property. The NFL placed him on the commissioner's exempt list on Aug. 30, shortly after charges were filed against him.

His status on the commissioner’s exempt list had prevented the three-time Pro Bowl selection from practicing or attending games. Players continue to get paid while on the commissioner’s exempt list. Upon request and with the club’s permission, they also can be present at the club’s facility on a reasonable basis for meetings, individual workouts, therapy and rehabilitation and other permitted non-football activities.

This announcement comes two days after Jacobs filed a lawsuit in Brown County (Wisconsin) Circuit Court against the Hobart-Lawrence (Wisconsin) Police Department as he seeks to have evidence in his case permanently sealed.

When charges were filed against Jacobs, the criminal complaint against him noted that a surveillance video from the camera system in their garage corroborated the woman’s statement. That video hasn’t been released.

The victim in that case already had requested that the evidence be permanently sealed. Clarence Duchac, the lawyer representing Jacobs in this lawsuit, said in his complaint that Jacobs “joins and supports (the victim’s) position that the identifying, private and sensitive records associated with the underlying incident should not be publicly released.”

The complaint also noted that public sports figures have recently been targeted for robberies and other related property crimes, and that releasing the video would reveal details of the garage’s interior that might put Jacobs at risk.

Jacobs was arrested May 26, three days after police officers came to his Wisconsin home to investigate a disturbance. According to police, the woman told them that Jacobs grabbed her and threw her to the ground as she was trying to exit a garage door, causing her to hit her head. Police said Jacobs also took her phone from her while she was on the ground.
Police said they noticed redness on her face and neck and could feel a bump on the back of her head.
Under an agreement Jacobs reached with prosecutors, the criminal damage charge against him can be dismissed in a year if he fulfills terms that include staying out of trouble.
Jacobs rushed for 929 yards and 13 touchdowns last season. He ran for 1,329 yards and 15 touchdowns in 2024 on his way to a Pro Bowl selection in his first year with the Packers.

Green Bay (3-2) has rushed for an NFL-low 60.4 yards per game so far this season while Jacobs has been unavailable. The Packers average 3.1 yards per carry to rank next-to-last in the league, ahead of only Las Vegas.

title: Lamar Jackson ruled out for 2nd straight week as the Ravens prepare to take on the Browns
summary: Lamar Jackson will miss a second straight game this weekend because of an ankle injury
story: Lamar Jackson will miss a second straight game this weekend because of an ankle injury
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Lamar Jackson is out again this weekend because of an ankle injury.
This year, there's no doubt who his primary backup is.

Tyler Huntley will have another chance to shine in relief of Jackson after the two-time MVP quarterback was ruled out for Sunday's game at Cleveland. Huntley won both his starts for the Ravens a season ago, and he also led Baltimore to an overtime win at Atlanta last weekend.
“The preparation and work that we do during the week (helps),” Huntley said Friday. "Just getting ready for the game so you can feel at ease while you are going through the scenarios.”
The Ravens ruled out Jackson, center Cam Jurgens (concussion), tight end Matthew Hibner (hand) and defensive tackle Broderick Washington (ankle) for this weekend.

When Jackson was hurt in Week 4 last season, the Ravens started Cooper Rush and lost their next two games, falling to 1-5. Then they switched to Huntley, who won a big home game against Chicago. Later in the season, Huntley guided Baltimore to a win at Green Bay as well — but the Ravens ended up falling short of the playoffs.

Last weekend, Baltimore overcame a late eight-point deficit and beat the Falcons 30-23. Huntley threw for 201 yards and two touchdowns. The man they call “Snoop” is a big reason the Ravens (4-1) are showing little panic as they await Jackson's return.

“He's a really good player, and he’s got a great demeanor. He’s got great poise. He has great respect amongst his teammates," first-year coach Jesse Minter said. “He’s just cool, calm, collected, confident — that to me, that’s infectious. When he’s in there, that’s kind of how the guys feel, and it’s really no different with Lamar.”

An undrafted rookie in 2020, Huntley made 10 starts for the Ravens — including one in the playoffs — through the 2023 season. That postseason start came at Cincinnati in January 2023. He played well enough to give Baltimore a chance, but with the game tied in the fourth quarter, he lost the ball on a quarterback sneak at the goal line, and the fumble was returned the other way for a Cincinnati touchdown. The Ravens lost 24-17.
Miami signed Huntley from Baltimore's practice squad in September 2024. He made five starts that season for the Dolphins and was with the Browns last year before being cut and rejoining the Ravens.
Since the start of last season, Huntley has been sharp when called upon, completing 78% of his throws and posting a passer rating of 105.6.
“We won’t bat an eye with ‘Snoop’ being in there,” Minter said. "We’ll go shoot our shot this week.”

This week's game is a reunion in more ways than one. Huntley faces the Browns, a team he spent time with during the 2024 and 2025 preseasons. And Cleveland's coach is Todd Monken, who was Baltimore's offensive coordinator the past three seasons.
“I’m more grateful and blessed to be where I am right now,” Huntley said.
Jackson was hurt while taking a sack near the end of the first half in Week 4 against Tennessee. He hasn't practiced since.
“It’s day by day, I would say," Minter said. "I think it’s just a decision for his best interest. That’s really what every decision’s always going to be about.”

title: NCAA sues Ohio governor over his executive order allowing schools to ignore new eligibility rule
summary: The NCAA has filed a federal lawsuit against Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine
story: The NCAA has filed a federal lawsuit against Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine

The NCAA sued the governor of Ohio on Friday, accusing him of trying to give college athletes in his state a “hall pass” to circumvent a rule that denies players who graduated high school in 2022 from a fifth year of eligibility.

NCAA President Charlie Baker called the lawsuit, filed in federal court in Ohio, an “extraordinary step” designed to prevent Gov. Mike DeWine from making it “impossible for all schools to compete on a level playing field.”

DeWine issued an executive order Tuesday that undercut the NCAA rule, approved over the summer. That and the NCAA's federal lawsuit in reaction to it marks the latest tit-for-tat in a torrent of legal maneuverings that are creating new rules on a state-by-state basis.
“This whole thing has become comical,” Danny White, the athletic director at Tennessee, said on social media in reaction to the NCAA announcement.

Under DeWine's order, public and private universities in Ohio would be able to allow the Class of ’22 athletes to play, even though the NCAA’s new guidance excludes those who have already played four seasons. The rule, passed in June, is the subject of multiple court fights.

In its court filing, the NCAA said it was trying "to halt a misguided attempt to give Ohio colleges and universities an unfair, unprecedented and unwarranted competitive advantage in stadiums and arenas throughout the country,”
“College sports, like all sports, depend on participants following the rules. (DeWine) is attempting to give Ohio institutions a hall pass to break the rules," the lawsuit says.

In reaction to the governor's move, the Ohio Supreme Court said it would step in and determine the legality of the executive order. As part of that, it paused an appeals court ruling in a case there that had declared the ’22 athletes ineligible. The court asked both sides to file briefs in the case, in which basketball player Filip Borovićanin is the lead plaintiff, by next Monday.
Baker said the NCAA did not believe the Supreme Court's order did, in fact, declare those players immediately eligible to compete and said it would submit arguments in that case.

That case, like others around the country, is becoming more urgent by the day, as it involves a handful of basketball players whose status for the upcoming season is in jeopardy. Among them: Gonzaga transfer Javon Bennett, Cincinnati's MJ Collins and Borovićanin himself, who played in an exhibition against Tennessee on Thursday night after DeWine's order put him back on the eligible list.

The NCAA has long explained that it knew excluding the Class of '22 from the five-year rule would cause those athletes hardship, but the decision was between them and the new class of high school recruits coming into college this year, many of whom would be displaced if the veterans were allowed another year.
Ultimately, the NCAA made its decision based on which move harmed fewer people.

The NCAA lawsuit goes through the history of the rule and the flood of legal actions that have come since. One of the original cases, a federal lawsuit involving basketball player Brock Wisne, is leaning in the NCAA's direction, though victories there have only spawned more lawsuits in state court.

“The results of this second wave of lawsuits were mixed, with the NCAA winning some and losing others,” it said. “But the lawsuits unquestionably destabilized college sports, with ever-more disruptive lawsuits challenging foundational rules at the heart of organized sport.”

During testimony in a similar case in Kentucky earlier this week, an NCAA attorney asked Louisville basketball coach Pat Kelsey why he was among those looking for Class of '22 athletes when the NCAA rules forbid that.

“From a coach's standpoint, every time the NCAA says something, we all shrug our shoulders and say, ‘Is that going to stand up? Is that a rule?’” Kelsey said. “We don't think there are rules right now. That's why we want guardrails, we want Congress to act, we want the chaos to end. Because nobody knows what the crap is going on. No one.”

The NCAA has long called for a federal law to tamp down on the lawsuits undermining its rules for hundreds of thousands of athletes across the country. The Senate has sent the Protect College Sports Act to the House, where its fate is uncertain in this election year.

title: Jalen Brunson may be small, but he wears a big target now after leading the Knicks to the NBA title
summary: Jalen Brunson doesn’t overwhelm anyone athletically like Michael Jordan or LeBron James
story: Jalen Brunson doesn’t overwhelm anyone athletically like Michael Jordan or LeBron James
NEW YORK -- Jalen Brunson doesn't overwhelm anyone athletically like Michael Jordan or LeBron James. He'll never overpower anybody like Shaquille O'Neal.
Brunson doesn't look like someone who would ever dominate an NBA game, which has left countless frustrated opponents wondering why they couldn't stop him from leading the New York Knicks to the top.

“That’s got to be hard, right? When you’re losing to somebody 5-10, 5-11, that’s got to be hard for you,” former Knicks superstar Carmelo Anthony said. “So I love the place that JB is in, because he makes people mad.”
Anthony was laughing, knowing that Brunson isn't quite that small. The Knicks officially list their point guard at 6-foot-2, 208 pounds.

But he's correct about the way Brunson makes opponents feel. Doc Rivers, stressing that he knows Brunson well so could say it with affection, shared what he thought while coaching against him last season in Milwaukee.
“How's this little fat (expletive) kid kicking our ass?” Rivers said.

Players who watched what Brunson did last season while leading the Knicks to their first NBA championship since 1973 clearly admire what the 2018 second-round pick has become. James and Giannis Antetokounmpo were among the superstars praising Brunson when training camps opened.

“It’s honestly really cool and it’s a sign of respect and to hear that from those guys, I really do appreciate it,” Brunson said. “But just like a lot of things, when you hear praise, when you hear negativity, it has to go through one ear and out the other and you’ve got to continue to be the best version of yourself or people are going to pass you. So I really do appreciate it. It shows where I’ve grown, but I’ve still got a lot of work to do.”

Brunson's postseason run took its place among the best in history. He averaged 28.4 points and became the sixth player to lead the postseason in scoring and then be voted NBA Finals MVP, a group that includes Jordan, James and O'Neal.

Once those players finally won titles, it was natural picking them to win again. They were the best athletes on the floor, or in the case of the 7-1, 325-pound O'Neal, the biggest. Brunson beats defenders with skill and not size, relying on footwork, fakes and spins that create angles to get his shot off against taller defenders.

“You look at LeBron, you see that specimen. You look at Michael. You look at Jalen and you’re like, well, can he keep it going?" Rivers said. "He’s not going anywhere. He’s going to be the same guy. He’s going to make the same big shots.”

Brunson's size — or lack thereof — was frequently cited by critics who said the Knicks couldn't win a title with him as their best player. Las Vegas Aces coach Becky Hammon, then working for ESPN, was among those when she said in 2023 that “if your best player is small, you’re not winning.”
Well, they won. Yet with Brunson as their leading man, the Knicks won't have the same aura as Jordan's Bulls or O'Neal's Lakers.
“We respect them, but we don’t fear them," Reggie Miller said, summing up how opponents would view the Knicks. "There’s a difference.”
And which side is the Hall of Famer on?

“I fear Jalen Brunson as a former player,” the longtime Indiana Pacers guard said. “I tell people this all the time: He is one guy in our game, if it’s close, he has such a clutch gene. He plays the game with such a maturity and he can destroy you in a number of ways in terms of scoring the basketball. And he just understands the game and how to win, so from a former player’s standpoint, I fear them.”

Anthony and Miller will be in Madison Square Garden next Tuesday night as part of NBC's coverage team when the Knicks raise their banner before facing Philadelphia in their season opener. Brunson will likely get the loudest cheers and probably chants of “MVP! MVP!” from fans who watched how he made his team the one everybody is looking up at.

On the other sideline will be the 6-9, 250-pound James, who at 41 still has the look of an NBA A-lister. Focus on athleticism, as Rivers said many mistakenly do, and it's easy to miss the beauty of Brunson's game and the impact it's had on a Knicks team that went 16-3 with a record victory margin in the postseason, right up there with anything Jordan's or O'Neal's teams did.

Derek Fisher, who played on the Lakers teams with O'Neal and Kobe Bryant that won three straight NBA titles from 2000-02, said the Knicks won more with their unselfishness and cohesiveness than individual talent, which are “harder things to quantify.”

“So it would kind of make sense that everybody wouldn’t necessarily, specifically fear Jalen Brunson in the same ways as they feared, quote-unquote, Shaq, LeBron, Kobe, Michael, those types of guys,” Fisher said. “But I’m not sure there’s any less of a reason to see them having a chance to come out of the East this year.”

Whatever talent evaluators thought that caused Brunson to slip to the No. 33 pick after winning two national championships and college player of the year at Villanova doesn't matter anymore. The superstars of the sport view Brunson as one of them.
“As far as what anybody says about JB, he is the guy,” Anthony said. “I think going into the season he is the top point guard in the NBA and he’s proven that.”
