title: Pope Leo discharged from hospital after lung cancer surgery
summary: Pope Leo XIV was discharged from the hospital on Saturday after undergoing surgery to remove a cancerous nodule from his right lung.
story: Pope Leo XIV was discharged from the hospital on Saturday after undergoing surgery to remove a cancerous nodule from his right lung.

The pontiff, who had been recovering at Rome’s Gemelli Hospital since Tuesday, walked out unaided before spending a couple of minutes speaking with well-wishers. He appeared to accept a gift of a homemade smiling Pope figure before getting in a car and being driven back to the Vatican.

“Following the conclusions reached by the medical team this morning, Pope Leo XIV will be discharged today from Gemelli Polyclinic Hospital, where he was admitted for surgery on his right lung,” the Holy See Press said Saturday in a statement, before the Leo left the building mid-afternoon.
He is expected to recite the Angelus prayer from the window of the papal apartment at St. Peter’s Basilica on Sunday, according to the statement.

The pontiff’s personal doctor, Dr. Luigi Carbone, and the head of thoracic surgery at Gemelli Hospital, Dr. Stefano Margaritora, said that in light of blood tests and a chest X-ray performed Saturday morning, and after an assessment of his clinical condition, “the Holy Father has been deemed fit for discharge from the hospital.”
So far, Leo’s doctors have given no indication that the pontiff might need any further treatment. And the Vatican has not indicated whether the cancer might have spread.
Leo, who is a Chicago native, resumed working from the hospital on Thursday, his doctors and the Vatican reported.

The Vatican on Friday released the first images of Leo since his surgery, showing him celebrating Mass inside the hospital, as doctors said that tests confirmed the “continued improvement” in his recovery.

The photos show Leo standing up at the altar in green vestments celebrating Mass in a makeshift chapel that has been set up for him. Spokesman Matteo Bruni said he presided alone over the liturgy, distributed Communion to medical personnel and Vatican gendarmes present and delivered a homily.
His discharge from the hospital comes less than a month before Leo is scheduled to jet off for a two-week trip to South America, which is set to start Nov. 11.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori, in an interview on Peruvian television, said the pace of the pope’s recovery could determine whether Leo makes his weeklong apostolic visit to Peru.
“I want the pope to know that here in Peru, millions of us are praying for his speedy recovery,” Fujimori said Wednesday.
Leo was diagnosed with adenocarcinoma, a type of non-small cell lung cancer, after doctors examined the nodule they had removed from his right lung.
Non-small cell lung cancer accounts for 80% of all cases of the disease, according to the American Lung Association.
This type of cancer affects both smokers and nonsmokers, although Leo is not known to ever have been a smoker.

The initial lump was detected during a routine check, the Vatican has said. The leader of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics took the rare step of revealing the health issue — the first of his papacy — during his Sunday noon prayer last week.
Leo waved to crowds outside Rome’s Gemelli Hospital as he entered Tuesday.
The procedure was led by Dr. Stefano Margaritora, Gemelli’s chief thoracic surgeon, with medical staff reciting the rosary prayer in the hospital chapel as the operation began.

title: 71-year-old man dies after alligator attack while fishing in Florida, police say
summary: A 71-year-old man died after an alligator attacked him while he was fishing, authorities said on Friday.
story: A 71-year-old man died after an alligator attacked him while he was fishing, authorities said on Friday.

Steven Hamilton was fishing at Dr. Bradford Memorial Park in Winter Garden, Florida — a city about 15 miles west of Orlando — when he was bitten by an alligator, according to a statement from the Florida Fish & Wildlife Conservation Commission.

Responding emergency personnel relayed reports that witnesses had seen someone possibly grabbed by an alligator and pulled into the water, according to a recording radio traffic. He was pronounced dead at the scene, the FWC said.
For Subscribers
The Winter Garden Police Department confirmed the incident in a statement, adding that FWC authorities trapped and killed the roughly 12-foot-long alligator.
The FWC said that “serious injuries caused by alligators are rare in Florida.”
For Subscribers
In June, a 31-year-old woman died after an alligator bit off one of her arms and mauled the other at nearby Little Big Econ State Forest.

“Always be aware of your surroundings. Always be safe,” Winter Garden police Capt. Michael Mason told reporters, according to NBC affiliate WESH 2 News. “Local wildlife, respect it, keep your distance. It looks like it’s docile, it looks like your Florida emblem, but it can be dangerous.”
Mason encouraged witnesses of the incident to reach out to authorities.

title: ‘The house was toast’: Surf swallows California homes
summary: The worst of El Niño is still months away, but Southern California’s fragile coastline is already being transformed by record-setting king tides and storm surges.
story: LONG BEACH, Calif. — It was 3:30 a.m. on Oct. 9 and the unthinkable was happening all around Shawn Curtis: The boardwalk in front of his two-story beachfront apartment building was gone. The 25-foot-wide sand beach was gone. Salt water poured in from all sides. And now the building was slanting down into the ocean.
Curtis couldn’t make sense of what he saw. “The doorframe was crooked. The window was crooked, and then I saw a big wave crash,” he told NBC News on Thursday.

The surf crashed all the way up to the second floor. Neighbors across the street said they could see water cascading down onto the roof of Curtis’ home of nine years. Booming waves were loud enough to wake him and shake his apartment as though an earthquake rippled through, he said.

title: Canada’s Mark Carney makes final appeal against Alberta separation ahead of referendum
summary: EDMONTON, Alberta — Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney made a final appeal to voters considering a path toward independence in his home province of Alberta on Friday, warning that a referendum is a dangerous gamble at a time of growing threats to Canada’s sovereignty.
story: EDMONTON, Alberta — Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney made a final appeal to voters considering a path toward independence in his home province of Alberta on Friday, warning that a referendum is a dangerous gamble at a time of growing threats to Canada’s sovereignty.

With U.S. President Donald Trump waging a trade war and threatening to make Canada the 51st state, Carney warned that the referendum comes at the “worst possible time” and urged Albertans not to take the outcome for granted.
“Don’t let anyone tell you this is already decided. Turnout will determine the outcome,” Carney told a pro-Canada rally in Edmonton, where he grew up.
“This is not a game. This is not poker. A vote against Canada is a dangerous bluff that will lead to years of deep uncertainty and lost opportunities for Albertans and Canadians,” he said.

Monday’s vote is not a direct referendum on independence. Alberta, home to most of Canada’s proven oil reserves — the fourth largest in the world — will decide whether to remain a province or instruct the government to begin the legal process toward a future referendum on separation.

Carney’s closing appeal came after two days of campaigning against separation in the province. Earlier Friday, the Liberal prime minister joined Alberta’s conservative premier Danielle Smith in a show of unity against independence.
Smith praised Carney for improving relations with a province that frequently clashed with his predecessor, Justin Trudeau, over his carbon tax and other energy policies.
“I think what we can agree on is that we have had some real change in the last 18 months,” Smith said alongside Carney in Red Deer, Alberta.
Smith noted that Carney grew up in Alberta and remains an Edmonton Oilers fan.
“He can’t be all bad, right?” she joked.
Trump’s threats raise the stakes
“Some outside our borders are working to break us so they can own us. Never. Never,” Carney warned Friday in Edmonton, repeating a warning he made a day earlier in Calgary.
At Thursday’s Calgary rally and Friday’s Edmonton rally, the crowd erupted in its loudest applause when Carney spoke about reducing Canada’s economic dependence on the United States.
Carney acknowledged Alberta’s longstanding resentment of federal energy policies.
For Subscribers
“Growing up, I remember how Ottawa made Albertans feel like our resources weren’t our own,” he said.
For Subscribers
But he also emphasized his deep ties to the province.
“Alberta is my home. I grew up here. This city, this province, this country have given me everything: my family, my education, my values,” he said.
Some Albertans say the vote shouldn’t have been called
Outside the Edmonton rally venue Friday, Alberta independence supporters waved flags and held a sign reading “Say no to Carney’s new world order.”
Smith called the referendum despite opposing independence herself. She recently cited a poll showing 22% of Albertans support separation, a figure she said was still too high.

Smith also faces pressure from separatists within her governing United Conservative Party. Former Premier Jason Kenney said the independence movement gained influence within the party as activists angry over COVID-19 restrictions, some influenced by conspiracy theories, embraced separatism.
But some Albertans who want to remain in Canada are angry with Smith for calling the vote.

“I think it’s a travesty really to be putting our province and our country through this when such a small portion of people are rabble rousing and saying they want to separate from Canada,” said Deb Lee, a retired Calgary resident who voted in advance to remain in Canada.
Smith said Carney had substantially addressed seven of nine federal laws Alberta opposed. She also cited cooperation on a proposed oil pipeline.
Independence advocate Tanya Clemens dismissed the agreements between Carney and Smith as “basically pinky promises” that came with too many conditions.
Political leaders unite against separation
Carney’s chief political rival, federal Conservative leader Pierre Poilievre, also urged Albertans Friday to remain in Canada.
“Don’t leave your fellow Canadians behind. Lock arms with them,” Poilievre said.

Despite their agreement on keeping Alberta in Canada, Carney and Smith remain divided over nine other questions on Monday’s ballot involving immigration and provincial powers. Smith wants voters to approve them, while Carney has urged their rejection.
“For the first time in a long time, Alberta and Canada are walking together,” Smith said.

title: Benjamin Satterley, wrestler known as Pac, died of bronchial asthma
summary: Benjamin Satterley, known to wrestling fans around the world as Pac, died last month of bronchial asthma, the medical examiner’s office in Cook County, Illinois, confirmed Friday.
story: Benjamin Satterley, known to wrestling fans around the world as Pac, died last month of bronchial asthma, the medical examiner’s office in Cook County, Illinois, confirmed Friday.
The manner of death was natural, the office said.
Satterley, 40, died Sept. 27, just one day after having wrestled on All Elite Wrestling’s “All Out” pay-per-view. His death sent waves of shock and grief across the world of professional wrestling.
The New York Post first reported the cause of death.
He was found in Des Plaines, around 2 miles north of the Chicago O’Hare International Airport, the medical examiner’s office said at the time.

Satterley came up through the British independent system before making the leap to Japan and the U.S. A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, he became a highly influential figure known both for his hard-hitting style and breathtaking aerial abilities.

He went on to earn global acclaim, wrestling for some of the top promotions in the world, including AEW, World Wrestling Entertainment (where he went by Adrian Neville), New Japan Pro-Wrestling and Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre.

Satterley adopted the moniker of “The Bastard” at AEW, and captivated fans and contemporaries with the speed, grace, precision and power through which he moved in the ring. On the microphone, his promos conveyed a no-nonsense intensity that equally gripped viewers.
At a time when the fourth wall between fan and wrestler had long collapsed, Satterley rarely broke character. Yet, his death highlighted the humility and kindness behind “The Bastard” persona.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
“He was just so modest about how fascinating he was,” Marina Shafir, a fellow member of the Death Riders stable of which Satterley was a part, said at an indie show hours after his death.
“I wouldn’t be here today if I didn’t share time and space with this man,” she said.
Days after his death, AEW turned its weekly “Dynamite” show into an emotional tribute to its fallen star, nicknamed “The Man That Gravity Forgot.”

“Whilst he will always have a legacy as one of the greatest wrestlers the U.K. has ever produced, we have been so glad to see so many wonderful tributes that acknowledged who Ben was as a person,” the Satterley family said in a statement read during the show. “He exemplified what it meant to be a decent human being, an honorable man with principles, who adored his family and his sausage dog son, Wolfie.”
On Instagram, his wife, Natalie, thanked Satterley “for our beautiful life.”
“We will try our hardest to get through this nightmare and look after each other as I know that’s what you would want,” she wrote, “but we will miss you every minute, of every hour, of every day.”

title: Zelenskyy says Trump is ‘rewarding Putin’ as he suspends Russia sanctions
summary: President Donald Trump waived sweeping new sanctions against Russia passed by Congress, arguing in an executive order Friday that the move “is in the national interests of the United States.”
story: President Donald Trump waived sweeping new sanctions against Russia passed by Congress, arguing in an executive order Friday that the move “is in the national interests of the United States.”

Trump had signed the legislation, named for the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, R-S.C., just last month. The bill took aim at Russia’s largest buyers of oil and gas, allowing the president to impose tariffs on goods from those countries, which may include China and India.

Passed with bipartisan support, the bill was intended to target Russia’s revenue streams as the country continues to wage its war against Ukraine. Suspending the sanctions provides Russia a financial lifeline.

Trump’s decision to put a hold on the sanctions package comes after he announced a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin last week to release hundreds of thousands of tons of Russian diesel fuel onto the global market as fuel prices soar.

Trump has expressed frustration with Ukraine’s attacks on Russian oil and gas infrastructure and has blamed them for the increase in fuel costs while downplaying the impact of the Iran war on the oil market.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Saturday that lifting sanctions was “wrong” and “only helps the Russians.”

In a Telegram post, he decried what he called an “American sanctions blackout,” adding that a “weakening of pressure on the aggressor, effectively serving as a financial reward for Putin—only encourages him to continue his attacks.”
“It seems to me that this won’t stop Putin,” he later told journalists in WhatsApp messages. “On the contrary, he feels joy and happiness that there is such support.”
The decision to waive the Russia sanctions drew swift condemnation from critics in Congress.
Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., called the move a “craven, cowardly action” in a statement.
“These waivers have nothing to do with our national security, and everything to do with sucking up to Vladimir Putin,” Blumenthal said.

“Beyond irresponsible,” Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., who is retiring at the end of his term, wrote on X. “What part of enforcing a law passed 86-11 by the Senate does the President and his advisors not understand?”
For Subscribers
“If the President wants to actually bring down energy prices, he can do it by solving the Iran problem, not by doing a solid for Vladimir Putin,” he added.
For Subscribers
Rep. Don Bacon, R-Neb., a staunch Ukraine ally who is also not seeking re-election next month, said “the president is prolonging the war, not ending it,” in a post on X.
“Lindsey would be appalled,” Sen. John Cornyn, R-TX, who lost a primary to a Trump-backed challenger earlier this year, wrote.
Zelenskyy thanked both Democrats and Republicans who supported the legislation, and praised the late Graham for his prolonged vocal support for Ukraine.

“He always supported us very strongly and pushed for as much assistance to Ukraine as possible. It’s difficult without him, I’ll say frankly,” Zelenskyy said. “And I am grateful to his friends who supported him.”

Trump’s move to pause the sanctions comes as the price of diesel fuel has shot up almost 70% since the war in Iran began in February and comes less than three weeks before the midterm elections, as cost of living remains a top issue for voters.

Sen. Darline Graham, R-S.C., who co-sponsored the bill named for her late brother, has touted its success as a key part of her campaign to win a full term in his Senate seat. Graham is a fierce Trump ally, as his endorsement was critical in her GOP primary win. Graham has yet to criticize the president for his Russian oil deal or the decision to halt the sanctions.
Congress passed the legislation with strong majorities in both the House and Senate, though many Democrats opposed the bill because it granted the president new tariff powers.

The legislation states that before the administration waives the new sanctions, it must submit an unclassified report to Congress explaining its basis. In his executive order, Trump said the White House has sent the report to Capitol Hill.

title: Immigrant ICE was seeking when it hit man with SUV has been dead since 2017, family says
summary: An immigrant rights group is calling for ICE to “come clean” about its pursuit of Jose Parra Hernández and to release bodycam video.
story: The person ICE said it was trying to detain when one of its agents struck a man with an SUV in Houston last weekend has been dead since 2017, according to an immigration advocacy group and an attorney who spoke with the deceased immigrant’s family.
ICE said that its agents were “conducting a targeted enforcement operation” to arrest Jose Mendoza-Cervantes when an agent hit and seriously injured Miguel Parra Hernández, 48, on Oct. 10.

In a previous statement, ICE said it attempted a vehicle stop and the two people in the car ran away. The officers tried to apprehend the fleeing men, and “Miguel Parra Hernandez ran in front of an ICE vehicle and was struck,” the ICE spokesperson stated.
The collision left Parra with hip, leg and ankle injuries, including a broken leg, according to his family and representatives.
Afterward, ICE issued a statement that included a headshot of the man it identified as Mendoza-Cervantes with the word “wanted” in capital white letters.
But the daughter of the man identified by ICE as Mendoza-Cervantes told an immigrant civil rights group that the photo was actually of her deceased father.

In a news conference Friday, the leader of FIEL Houston, Cesar Espinosa, said the daughter had identified the man in the photo as his father, José Hector Jimenez Mendoza, who passed away almost a decade ago while trying to enter the United States.

“She called our office sobbing because she saw her dad’s picture all over the news, all over the ICE website, saying they were looking for her dad,” Espinosa said. He added FIEL has turned over all relevant documents to Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare.

The New York Times first reported that Mendoza had died in 2017, stating that Mendoza’s daughter, Jamie Jimenez told the outlet the family was “horrified” to see their dad shown as a fugitive who was alive. She told the newspaper he used aliases, including the one used by ICE.

Parra’s attorney, Kim Bruno, provided a copy of a Mexican death certificate given to her and FIEL by the family. It lists the man’s name as J. Hector Jimenez Mendoza, his death year as 2017 and the location of death as Laredo, Texas. Several sections of the death certificate, which contains identities of parents as well as addresses and cause of death, were blacked out.
Bruno said the news that the man ICE identified as Mendoza-Cervantes is dead is “beyond mind-blowing” and the use of the dead man’s image is “jaw-dropping.”
Espinosa slammed ICE at the press conference and accused the agency of misidentifying the man with Parra.
“Either someone is not telling the truth or, all of a sudden, the two ICE agents have developed a sixth sense and are able to see dead people,” said Espinosa.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Espinosa called on ICE “to tell the truth. Come clean and turn over all body cameras.”
A senior Department of Homeland Security official told NBC News on Thursday it had bodycam video it was reviewing internally but a decision had not been made about releasing it.

At the press conference, Espinosa introduced the other man who fled with Parra, who identified himself only as “Omar.” He wouldn’t take questions but confirmed he was the person in the car with Parra before they fled on foot. The man has light-colored eyes, unlike the man in the picture that ICE issued.
ICE and the Department of Homeland Security did not immediately respond to questions regarding Jimenez Mendoza and about Espinosa’s comments.
Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare is investigating ICE on a possible aggravated assault with a deadly weapon charge as a result of Parra’s injury.

Teare, a Democrat, said it is “pretty obvious” from videos that ICE intentionally struck and ran over Parra. ICE has stated that “allegations that ICE struck Miguel Parra-Hernandez intentionally are RECKLESS and FALSE.”
Teare said he could take the case to a grand jury as soon as next week.
A senior DHS official told NBC News on Thursday that the officer driving the vehicle that hit Parra has been placed on administrative leave.
Bruno also is representing Luis Delfín Martínez, one of two men who were handcuffed in the back of the ICE vehicle when it struck Parra.
The two men had been arrested in a separate operation, Bruno and Espinosa said previously. Delfín, Parra and the second man in the vehicle, José Presa Cañada, are undocumented, Espinosa said.

Bruno said on Friday that Delfín suffered soft-tissue injuries from being tossed around the back of the ICE vehicle while he was handcuffed and not buckled in as it pursued Parra. Delfín is being detained in the Montgomery Processing Center in Conroe, Texas.
ICE did not immediately respond to a question about the allegations regarding Delfín.
Teare told NBC News on Thursday that his office had interviewed Presa at a south Texas detention center close to the border, and obtained “a significant amount of relevant details from him.”
ICE had told Teare’s office that it was planning to deport Presa, Teare said.

title: Selma Blair ‘did not intend to harm anyone’ in airplane incident, rep says
summary: A representative for Selma Blair came to her defense on Friday, just days after the actress pleaded not guilty after being arrested on two counts of second-degree assault in connection to a physical incident on a plane.
story: A representative for Selma Blair came to her defense on Friday, just days after the actress pleaded not guilty after being arrested on two counts of second-degree assault in connection to a physical incident on a plane.

The “Cruel Intentions” actor is accused of kicking a Port Authority police officer, and later a nurse at a hospital, after she was removed from the Delta Air Lines flight for being physically abusive around 11:50 p.m. Sunday, according to a court documents.

“Since Sunday night, the public account of what happened to Selma aboard a flight to New York has been built almost entirely on a police statement and a decade-old headline,” the representative said in a statement to NBC News. “We can, however, correct the record on a few points already in public circulation.”
The representative doubled down previous statements from Blair’s team that she “experienced a medical emergency on the flight” and that she “did not intend to harm anyone.”

Blair revealed in 2018 that she had been diagnosed with multiple sclerosis, an autoimmune disorder that attacks healthy cells in the central nervous system, according to the National Institutes of Health.

“What Selma has been able to do physically in the years since is nothing short of a miracle. She still has bad days, and she lives with pain daily,” her representative said, adding that the actress also has “pseudobulbar affect, a neurological condition secondary to her MS, which bears directly on how a medical episode presents to people who do not know her.”
According to the National Institutes of Health, pseudobulbar affect “may occur in association with a variety of neurological diseases,” including multiple sclerosis.
“For the same reason, she travels with a service dog who doesn’t leave her side, and the authorities took her dog from her,” Blair’s representative stated.
The representative added that there was “no attempt to open the door of the aircraft” during the incident.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Authorities in New York accused Blair of kicking an officer in the face, neck and chest when he was securing the actress on a stretcher to be transported to the hospital, according to a criminal affidavit in the case.
At the hospital, a nurse said Blair kicked her in the chest, according to the document.
In court, Blair’s lawyers said she had missed several doses of medication controlling severe neurological symptoms.

“There was an incident in which Ms. Blair actually fell and hit her head. These factors, your Honor, coupled with the altitude, resulting in a state of severe confusion and disorientation,” Shawn Barnes, Blair’s attorney said in court this week.

“There is much more to this story than has been reported, and we ask to consider the entirety of the facts before rushing to judgment, whether in the courtroom or in the court of public opinion,” the representative said.

title: Kindle, Away, Ninja and Hoka just dropped new products — here’s what we’re already loving
summary: Shopping experts tested new products from Samsung, Kindle, Hoka, Nutrafol, Oofos and more this month. These are brands’ best launches of October across categories.
story: This story is part of NBC Selected’s New & Notable column, where we highlight our favorite product launches. We will continuously update this article throughout the month with new releases we think you should know about.
Footwear, apparel and accessories launches
Hoka Arahi 9

Podiatrists we’ve talked to say the Hoka Arahi is one of their favorite stability sneakers for walking and running, and the brand just debuted its latest version. The Arahi 9, which is made with a little more cushioning for a slightly softer feel compared to the previous iteration, has Hoka’s H-frame stability system to prevent your feet from overpronating (rolling inward too much).

The brand upgraded the material on the sides of the shoe, making it tighter to give you more support, and added reflective details for extra safety in low light. You can get these sneakers in men’s and women’s sizes, and regular, wide and extra-wide widths.
Nike Hybrid RN

Nike created these shoes for people who cross-train, meaning they run and strength train back-to-back — for example, they’re ideal for CrossFit, Orangetheory or Hyrox. The sneakers, which come in men’s and women’s styles, have enough cushioning to absorb shock and keep your feet comfortable while running, but not so much that you feel unstable while lifting.

Their wide base gives your feet lots of contact with the ground to stay balanced, there’s rubber at the heel to prevent the foam from expanding too much during weighted exercises and the grippy, durable outsole makes sure your feet stay in place. The Hybrid RN also has an X-shaped overlay on the top of the shoe to secure your feet as you quickly switch moves.
Oofos Oocoozie Mules

These Oofos slippers blend recovery with coziness. They’re made with the brand’s signature foam and deep heel cup to absorb impact and keep you comfortable with every step, plus there’s a shearling lining for added warmth. “My feet are chronically achy and standing at the kitchen sink or stove leaves my back sore, too — these mules help ease that,” says NBC Selected commerce editor Bethany Heitman. “I wear them around the house and outside, and since they slip on and off easily, they’re perfect for my son’s shoes-off mommy-and-me gym class or a quick trash run. I also like that the fur feels stylish for fall.”

Tech launches
Amazon Kindle 6-Inch

The new 6-inch Kindle is Amazon’s most pocket-sized e-reader yet. A seamless flush-front design makes it lighter, while 16GB of storage, up to six weeks of battery life and 30 percent faster book opening keep you reading uninterrupted. It’s made with recycled materials and a 100 percent recycled cobalt battery.

You can also upgrade to a 32GB aluminum-back version with a premium matte finish. Along with this new 6-inch Kindle, Amazon just launched a new version of the Kindle Paperwhite and Kindle Papersoft, which are currently available for pre-order with shipping starting October 28.
Amazon Alexa Tablet 11

The Alexa Tablet 11 is Amazon’s new mid-size tablet, built around Alexa+ and wrapped in aluminum. Its 11-inch, 2.5K display runs at a smooth 90Hz and reaches 500 nits, making it well suited to streaming, browsing and reading. Inside, an octa-core MediaTek processor and 8GB of RAM keep things responsive, with 64GB or 128GB of storage. Dolby Atmos stereo speakers, dual microphones, a fingerprint sensor, Wi-Fi 6 and IP52 splash resistance round out the tablet.
The battery delivers up to 15 hours of video or up to 20 hours of reading, according to the brand. You can also add an optional magnetic stylus for notes and sketches.
This device is part of an entirely new slate of Amazon tablets, including the bigger-screen Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, the smaller, more affordable Alexa Tablet 8 and new kids tablets.
Samsung Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra

Samsung’s latest tablet has a 14.6-inch screen, faster processing, upgraded overall performance and a longer-lasting battery life, making it ideal for enjoying entertainment, making video calls and treating it as a laptop substitute. “I’ve been testing this for a few weeks and I’m amazed by how good movies and television shows look on it,” says Heitman. “It’s also fast and smooth, meaning that switching between apps never feels sluggish.”

The tablet, which launched alongside the smaller and lighter Tab S12+, also has multi-window view and comes with a stylus, and apps for creators like Adobe Photoshop and Pinterest come pre-loaded. There’s built-in smart helpers too, like Note Assist, which can tidy up your notes and pull out the key points for you.
Ray-Ban Meta Audio Glasses

Meet Ray-Ban Meta Audio, Meta’s first audio-only AI glasses. With no camera or display, they’re the lightest and slimmest pair in the lineup, looking like classic Ray-Bans in Clubmaster and Burbank styles. Open-ear speakers let you stream music, podcasts and calls without earbuds, while built-in microphones give you hands-free access to Meta AI, including live translation. Enjoy up to 12 hours of battery life, and there’s prescription-lens options.

Meta also recently announced that it’s adding Muse, a personal AI agent, to its AI glasses, and it debuted the Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3, which has better battery life and a slimmer, more comfortable design compared to the previous iteration, plus a customizable action button. You can also now pick from 27 color and lens combinations across three styles.

La Roche-Posay Anthelios UVDefense Sunscreen SPF 50

In case you missed it, bemotrizinol (also known as BEMT) is a newly-approved sunscreen filter that officially passed the FDA’s rigorous approvals process in June. BEMT helps to make formulas lightweight and invisible while still maintaining strong, broad-spectrum UV protection, according to the brand.

La Roche-Posay’s new SPF is a revamped version of the original Anthelios formula (which is a tried-and-true NBC Selected favorite) that includes the new ingredient. It has a lightweight texture that absorbs quickly with an invisible finish, making it a great option for all skin tones. It also includes an antioxidant blend that protects skin from environmental and free radical damage for up to 16 hours, and leaves skin hydrated for up to 24, according to the brand.
Nutrafol Strand Serum

Nutrafol is a favorite among our NBC Selected editors for hair growth, and this serum is the latest launch from the brand with a focus on protecting the hair you already have. The leave-in treatment is meant to reduce breakage and prevent split ends, according to the brand. Plus, it’s lightweight, so it won’t weigh down your hair.

“I like to style my hair with a blow dryer brush, which means my hair is full of split ends and breakage,” says NBC Selected associate social media editor Caitlin Cusack. “I’ve been using the Strand Serum for the last few weeks and have definitely noticed an improvement in my hair health, which has made styling much easier, and I’ve even noticed that my blowouts are lasting longer.”
Hero Cosmetics Mighty Patch Design Patches

Hero Cosmetics’ viral pimple patches are some of our favorite ways to cover a breakout and absorb gunk to help them go away. But with the popularity of pimple patches in the shapes of stars, flowers and other cute (and sometimes funky) designs, Hero Cosmetics has finally adopted the trend with these newly released patches. They’re kicking off with a limited-edition, holiday-themed collection, including patches in the form of peppermints, snowflakes and more.

Home and kitchen launches
Ninja Prepi

Prep and store ingredients with Ninja’s latest motorized kitchen gadget, the Prepi. It has interchangeable blades that let you dice, chop, slice, shred and puree, and then you can take off the PowerPod motor and serve everything inside the tool. It also comes with covers to store the food. To use the Prepi, you add whole ingredients to the chute and press down on them with the plunger, guiding them through the blade. Other than the blade, all parts are dishwasher-safe.
Windmill Space Heater

Most of Windmill’s home appliances are designed to keep you cool — until now. The brand’s newest product is a space heater that oscillates to distribute warmth across rooms and reduce cold spots. It operates quietly and has three heat settings, a timer, an auto-dimming display, a handle and a compact design that’s not an eyesore in your home. Plus, you don’t need an app to use it — just adjust its settings with the included remote.

The space heater also has numerous built-in safety features: The plug monitors heat levels and disconnects the power if needed; there’s overheat and tip-over protection; the internal components are VO flame-retardant; you can turn on a child safety lock; and there’s a plugged-in warning light.
Breville Spiral Luxe Auto Pour-Over

This coffee maker replicates the pour-over brewing method: It manually pours hot water in a spiral pattern over a filter with ground coffee at timed internals, which makes for an extra flavorful cup of joe. It has a built-in grinder that prepares coffee so it’s perfect for pour over, as well as a delayed auto start option. There are also customizable features, letting you adjust temperature, strength and grind type, for example. You can brew directly into mugs for smaller single-serve cups or brew into the 20-ounce carafe to make enough for a crowd.

Away’s iconic luggage just got an upgrade. The Series 3 collection has multiple new features to make travel seamless, including a built-in wheel brake that keeps your suitcase in place, a hook (on the handle) to hang an extra item like a jacket or duty-free bag, a dedicated pocket for your Bluetooth tracker and smoother, quieter wheels. The handle also adjusts to lock anywhere you want it; no more three-level height limits.

Both sides of the suitcases also now open outward, making it easier to see everything packed inside, and they come with the brand’s compression system to fit as much of your stuff as possible These new features will be available across Away’s classic styles (Carry-On 3, Bigger Carry-On 3, Medium 3, Large 3, and Trunk 3) and expandable Flex styles (Carry-On Flex 3, Bigger Carry-On Flex 3, Medium Flex 3 and Large Flex 3).

Away also launched its Signature Bags collection this month with five new styles: the Signature Companion Bag (which you can use as your in-flight personal item), Signature Tote, Signature Triple Zip Duffle (part briefcase, part duffel bag), Signature Weekender and Slim Commuter Backpack.
Bogg Go-Tote

The Bogg Bag is one of the most popular beach bags on the market, and after making dozens of versions and accessories, the brand now offers an additional bag: the Go Tote. It’s a lightweight everyday bag made from soft, flexible, water-resistant, easy-to-clean material. The Go Tote has a flat, durable, tip-resistant base, just like the original Bogg Bag, as well as top handles and a crossbody strap. There’s internal and external pockets for all your stuff, too. You can get the bag in three sizes: Go Little, Go Tote and Go Big.

You can now shop some of its most popular, recently refreshed pieces, like the hard-shell Aviator Luggage in four sizes (carry-on, carry-on plus, grand and trunk) and the Signature Canvas Totes. Period care brand Thinx expanded into apparel for the first time with these flowy, athletic-inspired shorts that have built-in, leak-resistant period underwear. title: ‘The house was toast’: Surf swallows California homes
summary: The worst of El Niño is still months away, but Southern California’s fragile coastline is already being transformed by record-setting king tides and storm surges.
story: LONG BEACH, Calif. — It was 3:30 a.m. on Oct. 9 and the unthinkable was happening all around Shawn Curtis: The boardwalk in front of his two-story beachfront apartment building was gone. The 25-foot-wide sand beach was gone. Salt water poured in from all sides. And now the building was slanting down into the ocean.
Curtis couldn’t make sense of what he saw. “The doorframe was crooked. The window was crooked, and then I saw a big wave crash,” he told NBC News on Thursday.

The surf crashed all the way up to the second floor. Neighbors across the street said they could see water cascading down onto the roof of Curtis’ home of nine years. Booming waves were loud enough to wake him and shake his apartment as though an earthquake rippled through, he said.

title: NYC college student dead after being drugged with fentanyl and raped in her dorm room
summary: A college student died after she was drugged with fentanyl and raped in a New York City college dorm room, federal prosecutors announced on Thursday.
story: A college student died after she was drugged with fentanyl and raped in a New York City college dorm room, federal prosecutors announced on Thursday.

The student, whom prosecutors did not name, and another unnamed student were drugged in a college residence hall in Manhattan in March, according to a press release from the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York. The other student survived the incident, prosecutors said.
Court documents show the women attended the Fashion Institute of Technology.
Two men were arrested and indicted in connection with the alleged crimes, according to prosecutors.

Moises Freire, 19, of the Bronx, was charged with distribution of a controlled substance with intent to commit rape, distribution of narcotics resulting in death and conspiracy, according to an indictment. Brian Peralta Cabrera, 18, of Queens, was charged with conspiracy to distribute narcotics resulting in death and serious bodily injury.
Both have pleaded not guilty. Lawyers for the two men did not immediately return requests for comment.

On March 18, Freire supplied one of the women with what he told her was “pure cocaine” from Mexico and “falsely” assured her that the drug he was providing did not contain any fentanyl, according the indictment.
For Subscribers
Prosecutors say that Freire knew that the drug, which he acquired from Cabrera, was fentanyl and had previously described it as “fake” and “poison.”
Freire encouraged the two women to consume the drug upon arriving to the residence hall, according to the indictment.

Both women “immediately” fell unconscious, according to the indictment. Prosecutors say Freire then raped one of the women while she was overdosing on fentanyl as the other woman lie unconscious several feet away.
After raping the unconscious woman, he took naked photos of her and sent them to his friends, according to the indictment.
For Subscribers
Prosecutors say Freire waited about 45 minutes before he contacted campus security, telling them the women were unconscious because they had too much to drink.
Campus security found the women and provided emergency medical care before they were transported to a nearby hospital, according to the indictment.
Only one of the women regained consciousness. The woman who prosecutors say was raped died “from complications from acute fentanyl intoxication” a few days later, according to the indictment.

“College should be a place where young people can learn, grow, and pursue their dreams, not a place where predators exploit their vulnerability,” said Christopher Roberts, who is the special agent in charge of the Drug Enforcement Administration New York Task Force Division.
“Every student deserves to feel safe, whether walking across campus, sitting in a classroom, or inside their own dorm room,” Roberts said.

Jason Schupbach, FIT’s president, said in a statement on Friday that all of the college’s “policies related to visitation in the residence halls were followed” in connection with the case. He said neither of the defendants was a student at FIT.

The college has reviewed its safety protocols and now requires certain staff members to “carry portable Narcan at all times as part of their uniform,” according to Schupbach. This new measure is in addition to Narcan kits stationed in the lobbies of the college’s residence halls, he added.

“What happened in March was devastating,” he said. “I want to reiterate that during those most difficult of days, we took swift action towards justice and came together as a community to support the victims and their families.”

title: Immigrant ICE was seeking when it hit man with SUV has been dead since 2017, family says
summary: An immigrant rights group is calling for ICE to “come clean” about its pursuit of Jose Parra Hernández and to release bodycam video.
story: The person ICE said it was trying to detain when one of its agents struck a man with an SUV in Houston last weekend has been dead since 2017, according to an immigration advocacy group and an attorney who spoke with the deceased immigrant’s family.
ICE said that its agents were “conducting a targeted enforcement operation” to arrest Jose Mendoza-Cervantes when an agent hit and seriously injured Miguel Parra Hernández, 48, on Oct. 10.

In a previous statement, ICE said it attempted a vehicle stop and the two people in the car ran away. The officers tried to apprehend the fleeing men, and “Miguel Parra Hernandez ran in front of an ICE vehicle and was struck,” the ICE spokesperson stated.
The collision left Parra with hip, leg and ankle injuries, including a broken leg, according to his family and representatives.
Afterward, ICE issued a statement that included a headshot of the man it identified as Mendoza-Cervantes with the word “wanted” in capital white letters.
But the daughter of the man identified by ICE as Mendoza-Cervantes told an immigrant civil rights group that the photo was actually of her deceased father.

In a news conference Friday, the leader of FIEL Houston, Cesar Espinosa, said the daughter had identified the man in the photo as his father, José Hector Jimenez Mendoza, who passed away almost a decade ago while trying to enter the United States.

“She called our office sobbing because she saw her dad’s picture all over the news, all over the ICE website, saying they were looking for her dad,” Espinosa said. He added FIEL has turned over all relevant documents to Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare.

The New York Times first reported that Mendoza had died in 2017, stating that Mendoza’s daughter, Jamie Jimenez told the outlet the family was “horrified” to see their dad shown as a fugitive who was alive. She told the newspaper he used aliases, including the one used by ICE.

Parra’s attorney, Kim Bruno, provided a copy of a Mexican death certificate given to her and FIEL by the family. It lists the man’s name as J. Hector Jimenez Mendoza, his death year as 2017 and the location of death as Laredo, Texas. Several sections of the death certificate, which contains identities of parents as well as addresses and cause of death, were blacked out.
Bruno said the news that the man ICE identified as Mendoza-Cervantes is dead is “beyond mind-blowing” and the use of the dead man’s image is “jaw-dropping.”
Espinosa slammed ICE at the press conference and accused the agency of misidentifying the man with Parra.
“Either someone is not telling the truth or, all of a sudden, the two ICE agents have developed a sixth sense and are able to see dead people,” said Espinosa.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Espinosa called on ICE “to tell the truth. Come clean and turn over all body cameras.”
A senior Department of Homeland Security official told NBC News on Thursday it had bodycam video it was reviewing internally but a decision had not been made about releasing it.

At the press conference, Espinosa introduced the other man who fled with Parra, who identified himself only as “Omar.” He wouldn’t take questions but confirmed he was the person in the car with Parra before they fled on foot. The man has light-colored eyes, unlike the man in the picture that ICE issued.
ICE and the Department of Homeland Security did not immediately respond to questions regarding Jimenez Mendoza and about Espinosa’s comments.
Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare is investigating ICE on a possible aggravated assault with a deadly weapon charge as a result of Parra’s injury.

Teare, a Democrat, said it is “pretty obvious” from videos that ICE intentionally struck and ran over Parra. ICE has stated that “allegations that ICE struck Miguel Parra-Hernandez intentionally are RECKLESS and FALSE.”
Teare said he could take the case to a grand jury as soon as next week.
A senior DHS official told NBC News on Thursday that the officer driving the vehicle that hit Parra has been placed on administrative leave.
Bruno also is representing Luis Delfín Martínez, one of two men who were handcuffed in the back of the ICE vehicle when it struck Parra.
The two men had been arrested in a separate operation, Bruno and Espinosa said previously. Delfín, Parra and the second man in the vehicle, José Presa Cañada, are undocumented, Espinosa said.

Bruno said on Friday that Delfín suffered soft-tissue injuries from being tossed around the back of the ICE vehicle while he was handcuffed and not buckled in as it pursued Parra. Delfín is being detained in the Montgomery Processing Center in Conroe, Texas.
ICE did not immediately respond to a question about the allegations regarding Delfín.
Teare told NBC News on Thursday that his office had interviewed Presa at a south Texas detention center close to the border, and obtained “a significant amount of relevant details from him.”
ICE had told Teare’s office that it was planning to deport Presa, Teare said.

title: Selma Blair ‘did not intend to harm anyone’ in airplane incident, rep says
summary: A representative for Selma Blair came to her defense on Friday, just days after the actress pleaded not guilty after being arrested on two counts of second-degree assault in connection to a physical incident on a plane.
story: A representative for Selma Blair came to her defense on Friday, just days after the actress pleaded not guilty after being arrested on two counts of second-degree assault in connection to a physical incident on a plane.

The “Cruel Intentions” actor is accused of kicking a Port Authority police officer, and later a nurse at a hospital, after she was removed from the Delta Air Lines flight for being physically abusive around 11:50 p.m. Sunday, according to a court documents.

“Since Sunday night, the public account of what happened to Selma aboard a flight to New York has been built almost entirely on a police statement and a decade-old headline,” the representative said in a statement to NBC News. “We can, however, correct the record on a few points already in public circulation.”
The representative doubled down previous statements from Blair’s team that she “experienced a medical emergency on the flight” and that she “did not intend to harm anyone.”

Blair revealed in 2018 that she had been diagnosed with multiple sclerosis, an autoimmune disorder that attacks healthy cells in the central nervous system, according to the National Institutes of Health.

“What Selma has been able to do physically in the years since is nothing short of a miracle. She still has bad days, and she lives with pain daily,” her representative said, adding that the actress also has “pseudobulbar affect, a neurological condition secondary to her MS, which bears directly on how a medical episode presents to people who do not know her.”
According to the National Institutes of Health, pseudobulbar affect “may occur in association with a variety of neurological diseases,” including multiple sclerosis.
“For the same reason, she travels with a service dog who doesn’t leave her side, and the authorities took her dog from her,” Blair’s representative stated.
The representative added that there was “no attempt to open the door of the aircraft” during the incident.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Authorities in New York accused Blair of kicking an officer in the face, neck and chest when he was securing the actress on a stretcher to be transported to the hospital, according to a criminal affidavit in the case.
At the hospital, a nurse said Blair kicked her in the chest, according to the document.
In court, Blair’s lawyers said she had missed several doses of medication controlling severe neurological symptoms.

“There was an incident in which Ms. Blair actually fell and hit her head. These factors, your Honor, coupled with the altitude, resulting in a state of severe confusion and disorientation,” Shawn Barnes, Blair’s attorney said in court this week.

“There is much more to this story than has been reported, and we ask to consider the entirety of the facts before rushing to judgment, whether in the courtroom or in the court of public opinion,” the representative said.

title: The Shocking ‘You Can See Everything’ Twist: Wait, Who Shows Up in the Elizabeth Holmes Documentary?
summary: The documentary about Elizabeth Holmes, “You Can See Everything,” takes a surprise turn that will have viewers on the edge of their seats. Here is what happens.
story: Spoilers ahead for “You Can See Everything,” the documentary about Elizabeth Holmes.
Thirty-four days before she was set to enter prison in 2023,Elizabeth Holmes let a film crew into her home.
“You Can See Everything,” directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, is the boundary-pushing result of what the filmmakers captured — and it’s unlike anything that’s been done before.

The Theranos founder and CEO hoped to revolutionize blood testing. However, in 2022, after a federal investigation uncovered critical violations in a Theranos lab, she was found guilty of four counts of wire fraud.

Sentenced to 11 years in prison, “You Can See Everything” shows Holmes in her San Diego home with partner William “Billy” Evans and their two children, Willian and Invicta. Maintaining her innocence, Holmes let the cameras film her and her family up until she surrendered to Federal Prison Camp Bryan in Texas.
But that’s just the first half of the almost-three-hour film.
What Is the Twist In ‘You Can See Everything’?
Amid the questions that arise about Holmes, as well as her relationship with Evans, Fielder decides to reach out to none other than Amanda Seyfried for insight.
Why the actor?
Seyfried portrayed Holmes in the 2022 limited series “The Dropout,” even winning an Emmy for her performance.

During his stay at their home, Fielder has Holmes and Evans watch episodes of “The Dropout.” The show ends up making Holmes uncomfortable and through tears she tells Fielder she no longer wants to watch it.
Holmes then goes to prison, but filming continues.

Holmes and Evans had been working on a new business venture, what they called Theranos 2.0. Two years after Holmes reported to prison, Evans calls the film crew and tells them he has an update on their project.
Fielder tries to get updates about Holmes, who was unreachable with cameras, but doesn’t get much. Then tensions start brewing between Evans and the film crew.

“As we are trying to finish making (the film) ... (Evans) started trying to exert a level of control over the process that made it very hard to engage with him,” Fielder said at an Oct. 6 Los Angeles screening. “It was uncomfortable for us ... We sort of had to stop. Communication broke down basically, and we’ve been in that state for a little bit.”
Fielder noted, at the time, that Evans had not seen the film.
How Did Amanda Seyfried Get Involved in ‘You Can See Everything’?
Fielder and Oppenheim had never met Seyfried, but was one of many people they reached out to in late 2025, according to press notes.
“A lot of people say no in this process, and a lot of people who are relevant to her story want nothing to do with her anymore,” Fielder said.
Thanks to a mutual friend, Fielder was able to connect with Seyfried, who agreed to watch their footage and talk about her experience on camera.

While preparing for her role in “The Dropout,” Seyfried never met or communicated with Holmes. However, the actor became “an invaluable key” in how the filmmakers continued their investigation and the “unprecedented” ending.
About halfway through the film, after Holmes is in prison, Seyfried and Fielder watch the footage of Holmes watching “The Dropout.”
This was the first in-person meeting between the two and it was captured “as it unfolded, unscripted and in real time.”
What came next is unorthodox, unconventional and intriguing.
Seyfried accompanies Fielder to Holmes’ San Diego home where he recounts the first time he met the biotech company founder. They then re-create that very scene.
As the documentary continues, Seyfried continues to help Fielder in his re-creations, including a meeting with the filmmakers, A24 executives and Holmes and Evans.
As Seyfried’s involvement deepens, she begins to bring her own perspective to Holmes’ life, also questioning the CEO and her partner’s intentions.

In a wild turn of events, Fielder brings Seyfried to Evans’ home, where she gets a chance to briefly speak with Holmes who calls from prison. After some shocking revelations, including Evans controlling Holmes’ social media accounts, the actor gets into a heated argument with Evans, cementing her dislike of him.
Seyfried also re-creates Fielder’s meeting with Holmes in prison, since cameras are not allowed inside.
As the documentary comes to an end, Seyfried and Fielder question if Holmes is a victim or they, too, are being deceived.

“I still am not sure to this day what I experienced,” Fielder said during the Los Angeles screening. “It’s one of the reasons I’m excited for it to come out and more people to see it because it was just a small group for so long. I actually think maybe it being out there, everyone can help me understand what I went through.”

title: What the Victoria’s Secret CEO Calls the Store’s Customers, and Why
summary: Victoria’s Secret CEO Hillary Super explains why the company has a very specific way of referring to its customers.
story: Victoria’s Secret CEO Hillary Super says the company has a very specific way of referring to its customers.
“I would say, especially our younger customers want an in-store experience,” Super, who has served as Victoria’s Secret CEO since 2024, told Savannah Sellers in a story that aired Oct. 17 on TODAY.
“There is this tremendous opportunity to be a third space for her and a gathering place where she can come and shop and have fun with her friends.”
The wording caught Sellers’ ear.
“It’s interesting to me to hear you using ‘she’ and ‘her’ about your customer, like we’re talking about an individual that you know,” Sellers said.
“Yes,” replied Super.
“One of our brand values is to put her first,” Super continued. “Everything that we do, we do for her. We read all of the social comments. I read them every single night before I go to bed.”
The Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show will take place Oct. 18, live at 7:30 p.m. ET on YouTube. It’s the latest move for a company that is trying to regain trust with its customer base.

Known for making superstars out of the likes of Heidi Klum, Tyra Banks and Gisele Bündchen, Victoria’s Secret found itself making headlines when it came out that former owner Lex Wexner had close ties with Jeffrey Epstein.
Wexner resigned in 2020, while saying he didn’t do anything wrong and he wasn’t aware of Epstein’s criminal activity.

“It’s not something any of us really want to be tied to, but at the same time, it’s important to know, know that bit of history to understand how far we’ve come and how much we’ve changed,” Super told TODAY.
There have also been accusations about poor treatment of models, including harassment and assault related to the Epstein era. That environment also led to change.
“We have very strict protocols in our casting, in our fittings, in any model interaction, and it’s actually monitored by a designated individual. So we’ve come a long way in that regard,” said

There have also been changes to the way the brand recruits talent for the Victoria’s Secret and Pink brands. “We like the mix of OG angels, new talent, sports figures, influencers. It’s about the mix of the community,” Super said.
“We’re really thinking much more expansively about who an angel can be, and to me that’s about self-possession, and just personal confidence, strength, and feeling great in your own skin,” she added.

title: All About Elizabeth Holmes’ Prison Sentence: When She’s Out
summary: As the new Elizabeth Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything” hits theaters, people are wondering when she will be out of prison.
story: As the buzzy new Elizabeth Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything” hits theaters on Oct. 16, the former CEO of Theranos remains behind bars.
The film gives an unnerving and intimate look at Holmes’ life with partner Billy Evans and their two young children in the weeks leading up to the start of her federal prison sentence in May 2023.
Holmes, 42, was convicted in 2022 by a California jury of wire fraud after siphoning off hundreds of millions of dollars from several high-profile investors and misrepresenting Theranos technology.

The Silicon Valley startup had claimed that it was going to revolutionize healthcare with a machine that could conduct hundreds of medical tests on a single drop of blood. Prosecutors said that Holmes knew the technology was faulty and still solicited investors and business partners like Walgreens — something she denied during the trial.
In “You Can See Everything,” comedian Nathan Fielder and filmmaker Lance Oppenheim spend extensive time with Holmes and her family.
A trailer released in September shows that Fielder moved into her house during the filming.
“I think this is the moment in time to capture this story before I’m gone,” she seemingly tells the comedian at one point.
Given Holmes’ backstory, Fielder asks her why she should be believed.
“That’s because I don’t have anything to hide,” she tells him.

News of “You Can See Everything” went viral after it was screened at the Telluride Film Festival in September, with attendees having strong reactions. Rebecca Keegan of NBC News Digital was among those in the crowd.
“There were audible gasps and ‘no ways’ consistently throughout this almost three-hour film,” she told NBC News correspondent Erin McLaughlin on TODAY Sept. 8.
The buzzy film also hits theaters three weeks after news broke that Holmes is expected to be moved from prison to a halfway house next year.
How Long Is Elizabeth Holmes’ Prison Sentence?
Holmes was sentenced to 11 years and 3 months in federal prison in November 2022, but it has since been reduced.
In May 2023, U.S. District Judge Edward Davila ordered her to pay $452 million in restitution to the victims of her crimes.
Also, former Theranos president Ramesh “Sunny” Balwani was sentenced to nearly 13 years in prison and three years of probation after being convicted of 12 counts of fraud.
Holmes has been serving her sentence at a minimum-security prison in Bryan, Texas.
When Will Elizabeth Holmes Be Released from Prison?

Her original prison sentence was reduced from 135 months to 123 months in March 2026 when a judge agreed she did not cause “substantial financial hardship” to her victims, according to a court document.
Her scheduled release date is now Feb. 22, 2030.
Holmes is also scheduled to be transferred from the minimum-security prison in Bryan to a halfway house in 2027, according to one of her victims. There has been no change in her release date.

Alan Eisenman, who invested about $1.2 million in Theranos, told NBC News on Sept. 24 that he was alerted by the Justice Department’s victim notification system that Holmes is to be transferred to the Austin Transitional Center. The halfway house is in an unincorporated community that borders Austin, Texas.

He said he has not received any money in restitution from Holmes that was part of the court ruling in 2023. Holmes’ attorney from her trial did not respond to a phone message from NBC News requesting comment.
Eisenman told NBC News he plans to watch “You Can See Everything.”
“She’s obviously manipulative,” Eisenman said. “If people don’t see that, then they’re blind. She’s the most conniving person I’ve ever met.”

title: Did the ‘Cheers’ Cast Drink Real Beer on the Show? George Wendt Revealed the Answer on TODAY in 1988
summary: “Cheers” star George Wendt spoke with TODAY in 1988 about whether he drinks beer on the show and what he hoped to do after the series ends.
story: Welcome to the “TODAY Archives,” where we revisit memories from our show when celebrities and newsmakers started discourse, made us laugh or shaped our culture. This latest installment features “Cheers” star George Wendt on TODAY on Dec. 8, 1988, talking about the success of the show in the middle of its lengthy run.

“Cheers” remains one of the most beloved and critically acclaimed sitcoms in history, thanks in large part to a stellar cast that included George Wendt. The late actor played barfly Norm, the unmotivated accountant whose love of beer and the bar trumped everything else in his life.

Wendt, who died in 2025, would have turned 78 on Oct. 17. He earned six Emmy Award nominations for his portrayal of Norm, coming in six consecutive years from 1984 through 1989, the heart of the show’s 11-season run, from 1982 until 1993.
“Cheers” was a massive hit, so did Wendt feel any pressure to perform for a live audience?
“You get to like pressure after a while. If you don’t, you’re really in the wrong business because there’s so much of it,” he told Gene Shalit on TODAY on Dec. 8, 1988.
Did They Drink Beer on ‘Cheers’?
Norm’s greatest love was beer, so did Wendt actually drink real beer while shooting his scenes?
“It’s not beer. It’s ‘near beer,’ which I guess it’s not available in draft or in kegs, so they pour cans of ‘near beer’ into Coca-Cola dispensers and out it comes,” Wendt said.

“They do that before the audience gets in and it’s flat and warm and just horrible by the time we have to drink it,” he continued. “In the first couple of seasons, I used to just be swilling it, be a real actor, sort of behaving as a bar patron onstage. Now, I have a feel for where the cameras are, and I only drink it when I’m on camera.”
Would There Be a Letdown After He Finished ‘Cheers’?

“Cheers” rolled with the punches with cast turnover, including the death of Nicholas Colasanto, who played Coach, and Shelley Long’s decision to leave after the fifth season. Wendt said there would be a “huge letdown” when the show wrapped up, but he missed the mark in saying that the end of the comedy was on the horizon.

“I can get sentimental right away,” he said. “I mean, we had so many reasons to be sentimental, anyway. When Nick Colasanto died, when Shelley left, and now, you know, the imminent end of the show — not all that imminent — but the end is certainly closer than the beginning.”
“Cheers” would remain a ratings juggernaut until its series finale aired in May 1993.
“It’s kind of a sobering thought that Norm might be the best role I’ve ever had,” he said. “I mean, it’s definitely the best role I’ve ever had. Might be the best role I’ll ever have.”
When Was the Last Time George Wendt Had to Pay for a Beer?
Wendt may not have had real beer on the set, but he certainly was taken care of whenever he was out.
“I know, it’s one of the great perks of employment history. I get free beer wherever I go,” he said.
“Too bad you’re not in the series where you’re a Cadillac salesman,” Shalit said.

While the role of Norm afforded Wendt fame — and free beer — he also wanted to keep acting in any form once his time on the show ended, whether it was TV or film, something he would do for the duration of his career.

“We just want to do good work, if possible, and the medium isn’t really important. Let’s say stage, feature films and television. The more you can spread it around, it really stays interesting for you,” he said.

title: Who Is Billy Evans? Elizabeth Holmes’ Partner Seen in ‘You Can See Everything’ Documentary
summary: Elizabeth Holmes’ rise and fall as the disgraced founder of Theranos is the subject of the new A24 documentary “You Can See Everything,” which premieres in limited theaters on Oct. 16.
story: Elizabeth Holmes’ rise and fall as the disgraced founder of Theranos is the subject of the new A24 documentary “You Can See Everything,” which premieres in limited theaters on Oct. 16.
The documentary, directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, goes behind the scenes to tell the story of how Holmes, 42, vowed to revolutionize blood testing only to end up a convicted felon.

After a 2022 federal investigation of Theranos labs uncovered critical violations, Holmes, who was just 19 when she founded the biotech company, was found guilty of four counts of wire fraud and sentenced to 11 years in prison.

“You Can See Everything” also delves into Holmes’ private life. The movie includes footage of Holmes with fiancé William “Billy” Evans and their two children that was shot in 2023 during her final days of freedom before she reported to a Texas federal prison.

According to the filmmakers, they revealed at a Los Angeles screening of the doc, Evans has yet to see the documentary. Fielder noted that after Holmes went to prison, Evans “started trying to exert a level of control over the process” that made it difficult to continue filming and “communication broke down.”

In February 2025, Holmes broke her silence to give her first prison interview to People. She described life behind bars, which includes two visits a week from Evans and their kids, as “hell and torture.”
“The people I love the most have to walk away as I stand here, a prisoner, and my reality sinks in,” Holmes said.
Read on to learn more about Holmes’ fiancé Evans.
Evans’ Grandparents Founded Several Luxury Hotels
In 1953, Evans’ grandparents, William and Anne Evans, founded Evans Hotels, a hospitality group consisting of several luxury hotels in San Diego, according to NPR.
Holmes and Evans Got Engaged in 2018, a Year After Meeting
Holmes met Evans at a charity event in Oct. 2017, she told People in her 2025 prison interview.
A year after meeting, Evans popped the question by presenting Holmes with a silver snake ring he bought at a Taylor Swift “Reputation” tour concert.
“I asked him 20 times if he wanted to spend his life with me,” Holmes said. “There were a million reasons why not.”
Evans Spoke of His Love for Holmes in a Pre-Trial Letter
Evans poured his heart out about Holmes in an emotional pre-trial letter to the judge in her case, reported The Independent.
In his 12-page letter, which also included photos of the couple, Evans wrote that he fell instantly in love with Holmes, whom he called “Liz.”
“I was captivated by her childish wonder and authenticity,” he wrote, adding “She listened more intently than anyone I had ever met.”
Evans praised Holmes’ vision, writing, “Her capacity to change the world is limitless.”
He also included the story of how Holmes competed in a Golden Gate Bridge ocean swim event in 2021 while pregnant with William.
“There were fifty reasons I thought it was a bad idea, the sharks, the tides, her complete inexperience swimming post age 14,” Evans wrote.
“You would think by now I would learn to not discount her perseverance,” he wrote.
Holmes and Evans Share 2 Kids
Holmes gave birth to the couple’s first child, son William, shortly before her fraud trial began.
She and Evans welcomed their second child, daughter Invicta, in 2023.
According to People, Holmes sat in the back seat of a Ford Expedition pumping breast milk for three-month-old Invicta as she approached the prison gates to begin her term.
Holmes ‘Always Wanted to Be a Mother’
While speaking to People, Holmes addressed speculation that she and Evans schemed to start a family to depict Holmes as more sympathetic so she might avoid time in prison.

“I know how the optics look, but I always wanted to be a mother,” Holmes said. “I truly did not think I would ever be convicted or found guilty. I kept talking to my lawyers and they also assured me we would never get this far.”
“It wasn’t planned and I can’t worry about what others think. It’s just when the timing happened,” Holmes added.

title: RJ Mitte’s Sister Pays Tribute To Late Actor: ‘I Not Only Just Lost A Brother, I Lost A Father’
summary: RJ Mitte’s sister Lacianne Carriere remembered the late actor as a strong support system who helped her during some of the family’s most difficult times.
story: RJ Mitte’s sister Lacianne Carriere remembered the late actor as a strong support system who helped her during some of the family’s most difficult times.

Carriere delivered a tearful, emotional speech, honoring Mitte at his celebration of life event on Oct. 16 in Brownsville, Texas, where he lived. It comes days after Mitte died by suicide, his representatives confirmed. He was 34.

In her speech, Carriere spoke about how Mitte ultimately became a father-figure to her during her earliest years, as their family navigated a devastating car accident that left their mother severely injured.

“R.J. Mitte was my older brother. But I not only just lost a brother, I lost my father,” Carriere told the crowd at Mitte Cultural District, an organization run by the family that hosted the event. “My mom was a single mother and when I was two weeks old, she was taken in an accident that paralyzed her from the waist down the first few years of my life, and my brother immediately took on the other role.”
Carriere added that “every part of me is R.J.”
“Every type of music I listen to, everything I watch, every game I play, our mannerisms — I just really miss my brother.”

The ceremony, which was live-streamed by the city of Brownsville, featured a number of speakers including his grandmother Anita Dianne Carriere, author M.J. Dougherty and publicist Nedda Soltani, many of whom shared sweet anecdotes about the “Breaking Bad” star.
Lacianne Carriere not only spoke about her connection to Mitte, but also her brother’s love for the city in which he lived.

“He loved Brownsville so much. He might not have been born or raised here, but this was his home,” she told the crowd. “This was his community. He loved it here, and he loved all of you, and he loved this city. And I want to thank you all for coming out.”
Carriere also shared a message for those who are struggling with their mental health.
“Please don’t feel like you’re alone. You’re never alone,” she said. “And just try, try to accept the help. Try, try your hardest, and just reach out to someone.
Carriere ended on an inside joke about her brother’s truck.
“And I want to say to R.J. I’m not going to sell that nasty truck,” she said, laughing. “It’s mine now. Thank you all so much for being here.”

Mitte died on Oct. 12, according to his obituary. His mother Dyna Carriere told NBC News that her son had no history of mental illness and never saw a therapist. However, she said that he had been going through a difficult emotional time recently. Still, he made no indication that he might end his life, she said.
“For the last three months, I’d been offering for him to go to therapy, trying to get him to go there, but he was like, ‘No, I’ve got it. It’s OK. I’m handling it,’” she told NBC News.

title: Carrie Preston Unpacks ‘Elsbeth’ Season 4, from Romantic Sparks with Smullen to the Arrival of Her Mom
summary: Carrie Preston tells TODAY.com what fans can expect from Season 4, including Elsbeth’s reunion with Kaya and a possible “will-they-won’t-they” romance with Smullen.
story: Elsbeth Tascioni has cracked some difficult cases over the years, but she’ll soon face one of her most challenging tasks yet: planning a wedding with her mother.

“Elsbeth” returned for its fourth season on Oct. 7 with an episode that hinted at where the whimsical consent decree lawyer’s storyline is headed. In “Crazy in Love,” Carrie Preston’s Elsbeth investigated a marriage counsellor named Serena Collyer, played by guest star Nicole Scherzinger, who murdered her secret lover.
To solve the case, Elsbeth worked with Detective Bobby Smullen (Danny Mastrogiorgio), who revealed he had recently separated from his wife.
Elsbeth and Smullen bickered about how to best handle the investigation and shared a brief moment where sparks seemed to fly between them.

While a new romance could be possible for Elsbeth this season, fans know for certain that one of the biggest plot points will be her involvement in son Teddy’s (Ben Levi Ross) wedding. She already seemed eager to help plan the nuptials in the series premiere, but the arrival of her mother could derail the happy occasion. When Teddy mentioned that his grandmother had been attempting to get in touch with his mom, Elsbeth’s usually cheerful disposition slightly dimmed.
Tony winner Christine Ebersole will play Elsbeth’s mother in Season 4, Variety reported, joining Uzo Aduba, Tyne Daly and more actors who are set to guest star.
Preston gushes that Ebersole is “incredible” in her role during an interview with TODAY.com.

“She really came in fully ready with the character, and we were like, ‘Oh, there’s mom. There she is! No rehearsal required.’ That’s the level of artistry that she brings to everything she does,” she praises.

The Emmy winner reveals that Elsbeth’s mom will add some tension to the lawyer’s personal and professional life, teasing that the premiere set the tone for the “complicated relationships” fans will see unfold.

Below, Preston opens up more about what fans can expect from Season 4, including Elsbeth’s reunion with Kaya (Carra Patterson) in the first half of the season, a possible “will-they-won’t-they” romance with Smullen and a current story dominating the news cycle that would make a great case.

It’s a dream to be able to even do a guest spot on a great show like “The Good Wife.” Then for that to have led to more appearances, and then to have led to appearances in a completely different show, and then to have a show centered around the character is very rare, and that rarity is not lost on me. The privilege is not lost on me. To be trusted with taking what was in essence a side dish and helping craft it into a main dish with incredible writers and an amazing showrunner like Jonathan Tolins and all of the incredible actors that I get to play with, has been really what I feel like I’ve been working for my whole life. So it means a great deal, which is an understatement. I’m also just excited every day that it’s something that people like yourself and audiences are enjoying and want to keep coming back for more because we’re having a great time doing it.

It’s been so fun to build her out as far as the people that she has relationships with. Because when we saw her as a guest star, she was the pinch hitter. She came in to hit the home run for the rest of that team. Now, she’s a detective. She was a lawyer before. We’ve seen her now on this show as a mother. Her son was mentioned one time in the entire universe of “The Good Wife” and “The Good Fight,” and now we’ve seen her as a girlfriend. This season we’re going to see her as a daughter. It’s fun to think about her in (relation) to other people. I’m excited to see where the writers are going to continue to take her as far as relationships, not just romantic ones.

That episode was so comedic and fun, and was also talking about relationships, setting up a season about complicated relationships. It’s definitely going to carry over as the season goes on. Teddy is getting married to Roy (Hayward Leach). Weddings, although they’re very joyous, sometimes bring families together in a way that can create some stress. It’s going to be fun to see what happens when Elsbeth’s mother comes, and we see a little bit more about the kind of upbringing that Elsbeth had, and the kind of mother that she was raised by, and parents. To learn about (why) Elsbeth wasn’t like the other kids growing up, and what that was like. Trying to fit in and all those things, which I think is going to just add more dimension and color to the character.

The thing that I love about our show is it’s not centered on a woman needing a man or feeling like a man completes her or she needs a man to make herself secure. Her primary relationship is with her work, and it’s with her son and her friends and reinventing herself at this age and stage in her life. That said, she’s someone who people are attracted to, and she is attracted to other people.

In the first episode, it was fun to play with the fact that sometimes you are attracted in a weird way to people that you are in opposition with. There’s sometimes a fine line between people who butt heads and people who kiss. Not that there’s anything going to happen with Smullen. I don’t know. I’m not in charge of the writing. But I do feel like it was a fun juxtaposition to what was happening with Nicole Scherzinger’s character in the episode.
